name: BrainCom
note: The company at braincom.fr in Bagneux appears to be a strategic-communications agency, not a neurotech company. The neurotech BrainCom is an EU research PROJECT at braincom-project.com. Worth a scope review against INCLUSION_RULE.

name: ApexNeuro
note: A neurorehabilitation CLINIC in Manchester (6 employees, Trustpilot-reviewed patient services), not a company whose product interfaces with or modulates the nervous system. No founding year found. Scope review against INCLUSION_RULE.

name: Accure Therapeutics
note: Develops CNS DRUGS (multiple sclerosis, Parkinson) from the Iproteos/Bionure merger. INCLUSION_RULE explicitly excludes companies developing drugs for neurological indications. Founding year written regardless; scope is a separate decision.

name: ableX
note: ableX healthcare Limited, Auckland, develops stroke-recovery products. Search returned the company but no founding year from any source; results were dominated by unrelated NZ rehab providers.

name: Aspen Neuroscience
note: Autologous iPSC-derived dopamine neuron replacement THERAPY for Parkinson (ANPD001) — a cell therapy drug, not a device or software interfacing with the nervous system. INCLUSION_RULE excludes drug developers. Year written; scope is a separate decision.

name: MedEngine
note: Two distinct companies share the name. MedEngine Oy, Helsinki, founded 2014, is pharma medical data science. MedEngine GmbH, Berlin, founded 2017, makes a Parkinson tracking wristwatch. Our record says Helsinki AND Parkinson, which matches neither cleanly. Needs a person to decide which company the row is. VERIFIED: medengine.fi is a pharma consulting agency (market access, medical communications), acquired by Voisin Consulting Life Sciences in 2023 — not neurotech. MedEngine GmbH Berlin, founded 2017, Techstars 20, built the Flytta Parkinson wearable and ceased operations around Aug 2023; that is almost certainly the company this row means.

name: Brainguard
note: A Berkeley News piece of Jan 2020 says BrainGuard was founded by Robert Knight eight years earlier, implying 2012. No source states a year outright. An arithmetic inference from a rounded phrase is not a sourced fact. A verifier additionally found Bicycle Retailer (Jul 2026) stating "Founded in 2011", which conflicts with the Berkeley arithmetic and may itself be aggregator-derived. Still unresolved.

name: Gaia Wearables
note: RIT alumni startup (Brent Chase, Joseph Clifford, Liam Herlihy), wearable for children with autism; founders graduated 2017 and coverage is 2018, but no source states a founding year. Now trades as Pal.

name: ALS Automated Lab Solutions
note: One source gives 1998 and another 2011, with nothing to adjudicate between them. Jena, Germany; CellCelector cell-picking platform; acquired by Sartorius in Dec 2021. Also a scope question: automated cell-picking for lab work is not obviously a product that interfaces with the nervous system.

name: Emotion ID
note: Camera-based facial emotion detection, not EEG or any nervous-system interface, despite the description in our index implying otherwise. Year written; scope worth checking against INCLUSION_RULE.

name: Brainwave Science
note: 2005 in some sources, 2012 in others, with nothing to adjudicate. Southborough MA; iCognative brain-fingerprinting for interrogation and deception detection. Also a scope question: marketed for counterterrorism, border security and deception detection rather than as a clinical neurotechnology. VERIFIED: the company FAQ says "In 2012, Brainwave acquired patents and exclusive rights to Brain Fingerprinting" — an ASSET ACQUISITION, not a founding. The About page gives no year, saying only the company was established in a post-9/11 world. The aggregators 2012 is probably derived from that acquisition line.

name: Perfuse
note: Perfuse Inc, Los Angeles, AI for stroke care. Crunchbase lists the company but gives no founding year. Two similarly named companies exist and are NOT this one: Perfuse Therapeutics (San Francisco, 2018, ocular) and Perfusio (Greenville NC, 2016, burn imaging).

name: Neuronoff
note: I wrote 2013 from Tracxn. A four-year spread from aggregators alone is not a fact.

They are one company, and audit-duplicate-orgs.js CANNOT find this: it matches on normalised names, and a rename shares no letters. Found only because a verifier noted that Onward was founded under the G-Therapeutics name. Left in place; merging two rows is a decision about which /company/:id stops working.

name: Bellabee
note: Wearable neurofeedback headband. No source states a founding year; results are dominated by Bellabeat, a different company (women health tracker) with a near-identical name. Our record says Austin; product pages point to bellabee.pro. VERIFIED: no primary source gives a year, and Bellabee appears to be a rebrand or successor of the earlier ELF Emmit headband, so any date found may belong to a predecessor entity.

name: Membean
note: Vocabulary learning software for schools (durable learning). No product interfacing with, measuring or modulating the nervous system. Fails INCLUSION_RULE on its face; not searched for a year.

name: Skoolbo Pte Ltd
note: Childrens literacy and numeracy learning games. Not neurotechnology under INCLUSION_RULE; not searched for a year.

name: Mindsail
note: Wellness app with on-demand programmes. No nervous-system interface; fails INCLUSION_RULE on its face.

name: SuperBetter
note: Digital wellbeing gamification. No nervous-system interface; fails INCLUSION_RULE on its face.

name: Mentalico

name: Sensory Innovation Solutions
note: Stored website is the literal string https://N/A, so there is no site to check and the name is too generic to search reliably. The bad website value is itself worth fixing.

name: Cerebian

Year cleared.

name: Atlas
note: Our row points at atlasmh.com, which an agent found is a teen wellness journaling and podcast app, now a generic mental-health content hub, marked permanently closed. If the index means that one, this row has the wrong website, the wrong description and the wrong company.

name: Singular Hearing
note: BC Corporate Registry shows SINGULAR HEARING INC registered 1 Aug 2022, but the venture was publicly named in Dec 2019 press ahead of CES 2020 as a subsidiary of Singular Software, so the registration post-dates it. No primary source states a founding year. SCOPE: smartphone audio DSP and speech separation, no neural interface.

name: Go Go Games Studios
note: iPad matching games translating behavioural autism therapy. No sensing or stimulation of the nervous system. Year written regardless.

name: Preventicus
note: Smartphone and smartwatch PPG pulse-wave analysis for atrial fibrillation. Cardiovascular, not nervous system. Year written regardless.

name: Neuregenix
note: Preclinical contract research organisation running CNS and PNS injury models and axon-regeneration assays for drug discovery. A research service, not a device. Dissolved Jan 2025.

name: Accure Health
note: Liquid-biopsy and exosome nanosensing diagnostics for cancer and immune response. No nervous-system measurement or modulation.

name: Sleepmed
note: Measures the nervous system via polysomnography and ambulatory EEG, but operates as a diagnostic service and sleep-lab network rather than a technology developer.

name: Biotic
note: BIOTIC is the BIOmedical Translational Imaging Centre, a hospital and university research facility embedded in the IWK and QEII Health Sciences Centre and listed by the Canada Foundation for Innovation under Dalhousie University. No founding year appears on any archived page or brochure; the widely repeated 2013 could not be traced to any actual source. Should probably leave the index.

name: MyLeg
note: MyLeg is EU Horizon 2020 grant agreement 780871, coordinated by Rijksuniversiteit Groningen, running 1 Jan 2018 to 28 Feb 2023 with Bologna, Twente, Roessingh, Radboud UMC and Ossur. The 2018 date is a PROJECT START and must not be recorded as a founding year. The underlying implantable myoelectric sensor work would otherwise qualify.

name: Mind Layer
note: Every archived capture (Mar 2021 to Jul 2022) is a JavaScript-only React shell whose entire body is a noscript message, and the Archive never captured the JS, so there is no About text to read. No press, register or institutional source for a biomedical-data-analysis Mind Layer could be found. The domain today serves an unrelated Korean parenting blog. Beware namesakes: MindLayer Ltd Hong Kong, mindlayer.io, Mind Layers AI.

name: NeuroCrowd
note: The only substantive archived capture (Apr 2014) describes an EEG, eye-tracking and facial-recognition neuromarketing panel but states no founding year. It gives a MEXICO CITY address (WTC Mexico DF), contradicting the Houston location in our index. The site was a parking page by 2018 and the company is almost certainly defunct. Domain created 2013-08-22, which is registration not founding.

name: FK Biotecnologia
note: Autologous cancer immunotherapy and human immunodiagnostics — a drug developer with no nervous-system interface. Year written regardless.

name: Woebot

name: Humachina
note: Lucidity Insights and PitchBook both give 2017; the company own site states no year. SCOPE: AI career-coaching and personalised-learning platform, no nervous-system measurement.

name: Optimal Medical Therapies
note: Home infusion therapy provider and pump supplier, part of VitalAire/Air Liquide. The only neuro-adjacent item is a discontinued RF electrode and generator for pain. Year written regardless.

name: Neuralis

name: infiBond

name: Chronaly Inc.
note: Mobile logging and tracking app for autism and developmental disabilities. No nervous-system interface. Domain dead, company closed.

name: Emotional ABCs
note: Childrens social-emotional learning curriculum. General education software; fails INCLUSION_RULE.

note: Software-only olfactory test scoring smell loss as an early Parkinson or Alzheimer biomarker. Measures a nervous-system function but has no hardware interface, and sits close to the diagnostic-service exclusion. Ceased operations.

name: Sim&Cure
note: Patient-specific simulation and sizing software for endovascular aneurysm devices. Cerebrovascular, not a neural interface.

name: Filterlex Medical
note: Aortic embolic protection filter for TAVR. Prevents stroke but does not interface with, measure or modulate the nervous system.

name: Lumendo
note: Light-cured injectable implant fillers for dental and bone, with claimed spinal applications. Primary product is not a neural interface.

name: MindPlay

name: Neurocern
note: Web-based dementia care management and predictive analytics for insurers. Records and claims analytics, no nervous-system interface.

name: ALA Diagnostics
note: ELISA-based in vitro blood test for multiple sclerosis. Assays a blood analyte; does not interface with or measure the nervous system itself.

name: BrainTalk
note: Only a description surfaced: speech-sample detection of cognitive deficits, a collaboration between Israel National Institute for the Rehabilitation of the Brain Injured and US firm SentiMetrix. name: Tivic Health

name: Therapy-Box
note: AAC, text-to-speech and speech-therapy apps. Assistive software with no nervous-system interface or measurement.

name: Clara Biotech
note: Microfluidic exosome isolation instrumentation for lab and diagnostic sample prep. No nervous-system interface. Reportedly acquired by InnovaPrep in Oct 2023.

name: Zed Medical
note: Our row says cerebral aneurysm embolic device. zedmedical.com describes a dual-mode CORONARY catheter combining FFR pressure and IVUS ultrasound for cardiac intervention — there is no cerebral aneurysm product on the site. The year is also unsettled: aggregators say 2016, the California register shows a filing date of 6 Feb 2023, and a ZED Medical led by Tom Moore was seed-funded in 2018 for intra-body imaging catheters.

name: NBI Development
note: A 4 Dec 2006 release announces a $5.5M SEED round — a funding event, not a founding. It says the company was founded by Mayo Clinic, Bay City Capital and the Venturi Group but gives no year. CEO Konstantinos Alataris went on to lead Nevro, generally dated to 2006 out of the same effort, which is suggestive but not confirmation.

name: The Virtual Brain
note: An open-source neuroinformatics and simulation project run by an academic consortium founded by Viktor Jirsa (Aix-Marseille), Randy McIntosh (Baycrest Toronto) and Petra Ritter (Charite Berlin), funded largely by the James S. McDonnell Foundation and now hosted on the EU EBRAINS platform. No founding year is stated; the flagship papers appeared in 2013. Toronto is ONE OF THREE consortium sites, not a company HQ.

name: Limbix
note: SparkRx is self-guided CBT software with no sensing or modulation of the nervous system. Acquired by Big Health July 2023; domain dead.

name: Impulse Monitoring
note: Outsourced intraoperative neuromonitoring SERVICE, staffing neurophysiologists for surgery, rather than a product company. Absorbed into NuVasive Clinical Services in 2011; domain dead.

name: Sensoree
note: The company own About page gives no founding year, saying only that SENSOREE began as Future Speculation for Healthcare from Master Thesis design research by Kristin Neidlinger. Press coverage runs 2013-2014 and never states a year. SCOPE: biosensing affective wearables reading galvanic skin response, i.e. autonomic arousal — arguably in scope.

name: DeepBrainz
note: The only date is an INCORPORATION: DeepBrainz Technologies Private Limited, 18 Nov 2019, ROC Bangalore. No About page or press statement gives a founding year. SCOPE: general enterprise AI cloud and edge-to-cloud services — nothing neural despite the name.

name: Amind
note: The company Nosotros page gives no founding year. The only year on the site belongs to its Swedish PARTNER Livanda, founded 2001. The site presents as a Spanish-language operation, not the San Ramon USA our index records. SCOPE: internet-delivered CBT with a psychologist, a therapy service.

name: Lucid Care
note: Aggregators give 2017 with founders Yahav Tako and Rebecca Mandel Ben-Artzy, based in PALO ALTO, not the Los Angeles we record, with a VR digital therapeutic for addiction. But lucid.care today is Lucid.Care Labs Inc selling a mental-health symptom-tracking app with wearable integration and NO VR anywhere. The two may not be the same entity, so no year was written.

note: Optogenetic gene therapy developer using AAV-delivered opsins. Excluded as a gene-therapy developer.

note: GPS trackers and wearable vital-sign monitors (OiX Care for Alzheimer patients, PaciBreath infant pacifier). No nervous-system measurement or modulation.

name: Resproly

note: Online therapy and medication management. A care provider, not neurotechnology. Recorded separately after this and five others were wrongly filed as a single entry under one comma-joined name, which no name lookup could ever match.

note: neuroscientia.com is live but is a general health and lifestyle content blog, Your Pocket Health Care, whose contact address is GuestPost@GeniusUpdates.com — the hallmark of a link-selling content farm. note: Manufactures behavioural testing apparatus (mazes) for rodents — measures behaviour, not the nervous system. The domain now redirects to conductscience.com, so it is a product line under the ConductScience brand rather than a standalone company.

name: Ornim Medical

note: ACTIVATE is Yale-derived computerised cognitive and executive-function training for ADHD. Software-based training with no sensing or modulation hardware, so it sits close to the general education software exclusion.

This is the second rename-duplicate found (after G-Therapeutics/Onward Medical) and again invisible to name matching. incereb.ie is now dead.

name: NeuroChat
note: Russian register: OOO NeuroChat, INN 7730203648, registered 19.05.2016, Moscow Skolkovo, director N.V. Galkina. One of the first NeuroNet projects of the Russian National Technology Initiative. Consistent with 2016 but never stated as a founding.

name: Your Brain Training

SCOPE: content marketing and coaching, not a product company.

note: classicattention.com does not resolve at all. No About page, no company entity, no incorporation record. The product was built on Google Glass, discontinued in 2015. SCOPE: behaviour modification software delivering pre-recorded teacher praise on a reinforcement schedule; neither measures nor modulates the nervous system.

name: Clearhead
note: AI triage chatbot and therapist-matching platform. No nervous-system measurement or modulation; a mental-health service marketplace.

name: Elevatr
note: Peer-and-counsellor chat marketplace for depression and anxiety. No nervous-system interface.

name: Garlew
note: Self-reflection and journaling app for addiction, anxiety and negativity, plus a workplace engagement platform. Psychology-informed software with no nervous-system measurement.

note: BioMind is the product; the company is Hanalytics Pte Ltd, Singapore. SCOPE: AI diagnostic software over brain MRI and CT — it analyses neuroimaging but does not interface with or modulate the nervous system.

name: Carl Zeiss
note: A general optics, semiconductor and metrology conglomerate founded 1846. Its nervous-system-adjacent products, chiefly surgical microscopes, are a minor line rather than the primary product.

name: Ginger
note: Teletherapy and coaching service provider — behavioural health care delivery, not neurotechnology. Merged into Headspace Health in 2021.

name: MyndVR
note: myndvr.com redirects to myndimmersive.com; the company now trades as Mynd Immersive. SCOPE: VR sensory content for older adults, therapeutic intent but no neural measurement or modulation.

note: A smartphone app, not a company: self-reported ALSFRS-R plus speech and motor tasks, built by the nonprofit Prize4Life (US 501(c)(3), EIN 20-5055664, founded 2007 by Avi Kremer). name: Nisensor
note: nisensor.com and nisensor.net both fail DNS resolution. The only live presence is an unclaimed Webflow staging subdomain. No founding year in any source. The name also collides with NISensors.com (iWorx lab instrumentation) and with NiSensor-1, a nickel fluorescent probe from the chemistry literature. Probably defunct.

name: Temari Medical
note: temarimd.com does not resolve. A cerebral aneurysm device company (Enfold, Divera) spun out of the Adventus Ventures incubator; the only dated source is a May 2018 seed financing release, which is a funding date. name: Radar Vision
note: radarvision.org fails TLS: the certificate is issued for gloryraks.com, so the domain now points at unrelated parked or resold hosting. The two aggregator descriptions contradict each other, one calling it police computer-vision analytics and the other Bluetooth 5 sensors, and neither is neurotechnology. A Cape Town neurotech entity of this name could not be shown to exist. Candidate for removal.

name: Mobio Interactive
note: Sources give 2014 and 2015, with a LinkedIn-derived profile suggesting a founding advisor role from February 2012. No primary source resolves it and the company site states no year. The entity is Mobio Interactive Inc.; MI Digital Therapeutics is a brand and Am Mindfulness the product. A spin-off of the Vision and Image Processing group at University of Waterloo. SCOPE: software-only stress and mental-health app with no hardware. LOCATION: most current sources place it in Singapore, not Toronto.

name: Health Safe Today
note: Only an incorporation date exists: 27 Dec 2019, CIN U85100DL2019PTC359430. Three further problems. The domain fails DNS resolution. The registered address is D-1/8 Vasant Vihar, New Delhi, not Mumbai as the index records. name: Ocuspecto Oy
note: Finnish trade register records registration on 11 May 2012, business ID 2478157-7 — an incorporation date, not a founding. name: Neurofus
note: NeuroFUS is a product line for low-intensity transcranial focused ultrasound neuromodulation (NeuroFUS PRO, CTX and DPX systems). neurofus.com states it is powered by Sonic Concepts, Inc. of Bothell, Washington, which matches the location in the index. Sonic Concepts was founded in 1989 by George Keilman as an ultrasound transducer consultancy; some databases say 1986. The founding year therefore belongs to a company the index does not name. Re-key this row to Sonic Concepts and the 1989 year can be written.

name: Shimojani
note: A preclinical drug company, not neurotech: it licensed an invention from Niigata University to reduce hemorrhagic transformation risk in stroke patients treated with tPA, and is in IND-enabling development. No device, interface or hardware. shimojani.com is a bare WordPress install whose only post is a Hello World dated 28 January 2025. Location is unstable across sources, San Francisco in one and Pray, Montana in another. Existed by February 2013, when it announced the Niigata licence; that is a licensing event, not a founding.

name: Mindful Scientific
note: The widely repeated 2009 is the year the Halifax Consciousness Scanner was prototyped by Ryan C.N. D'Arcy and Don Weaver — a device milestone bleeding into company records, not a founding. Entrevestor (24 Oct 2014) says only that Tam "became CEO less than three years ago", a role start, and arithmetic on it is forbidden. The duplicated path segment in the URL is genuinely how the site was published, but the host repeatedly failed to complete a connection, so it is at best flaky. Co-inventor D'Arcy later founded HealthTech Connex, so watch for related-entity confusion.

name: Cyberonics
note: Year recorded as 1987. The company no longer exists under this name: it merged with Sorin S.p.A. on 19 October 2015 in a $2.7B deal forming LivaNova PLC. The Houston address in the index survives as LivaNova North American operational HQ at 100 Cyberonics Blvd. The index should carry LivaNova as current name with Cyberonics as the historical entity.

name: Tactx Medical
note: Year recorded as 2003. Creganna acquired the company in January 2010, trading as Creganna-Tactx Medical, and that business was later rolled into TE Connectivity; tactxmed.com is stale. SCOPE: a contract designer and manufacturer of catheters and delivery systems across cardiology, urology, GI and optometry, with neurology one market among many.

name: Concrn
note: Year recorded as 2014. A nonprofit community crisis-response service dispatching trained compassionate responders to behavioural-health crises, mainly in San Francisco Tenderloin. TechCrunch calls it a non-profit startup and its own framing is a civilian alternative to calling 911. There is no neurotechnology in it.

name: Medlink Neurology
note: Year recorded as 1992. This is a subscription clinical reference publication of roughly 1,200 peer-reviewed neurology condition monographs, published by MedLink Corporation of San Diego. It has an ISSN, 2831-9125, which is the signature of a periodical rather than a device or software company. The index records no location; it is San Diego. Reclassify as a medical publisher or remove.

name: XEED
note: Year recorded as 2016. The company began as a Parkinson tremor-monitoring wearable out of Penn Engineering, but xeedlimits.com now markets full-body analytics for at-home fitness — motion capture for yoga, weightlifting and sports. The medical and neuro framing is largely historical.

name: Synappse Assist
note: Year recorded as 2017. A mental-health symptom-tracking mobile app covering symptom monitoring, side effects, medication reminders and exam records. Not neurotechnology in any hardware or neural-interface sense.

name: Babbly
note: Year recorded as 2018, the best-sourced year in its batch. But the product is a machine-learning child speech and language development tracking app for parents: digital health rather than neurotechnology.

name: foc.us
note: Year recorded as 2012. The site states foc.us is owned and operated by Brain Control Co., so the row is a brand and the legal entity is a company the index never names. Consumer transcranial stimulation devices — tDCS, tACS, tPCS, tRNS — founder Michael Oxley. Site is live.

name: Tovertafel (Active Cues)
note: Year recorded as 2015. Tovertafel is the product, an interactive light-projection game for dementia and disability care. The company was Active Cues and has since renamed to Tover; the legal entity per its own site is Tover Health Tech B.V. tovertafel.com now redirects to tover.care. In scope, though it acts through sensory and behavioural engagement rather than directly on the nervous system.

name: AgenT
note: Year recorded as 2018. A blood-based multiomics and machine-learning diagnostic (B-HEALED, B-AHEAD) predicting Alzheimer progression before symptoms. An in-vitro diagnostic with an algorithm: no device, hardware or software acting on the nervous system. Neuro-adjacent by indication only.

name: Biocross
note: Year recorded as 2005. A CSIC spin-off in the Boecillo technology park developing blood-based biomarker tests to diagnose Alzheimer and discriminate between dementias. Same category as AgenT: in-vitro diagnostics, not neurotechnology.

name: CubeHX
note: Year recorded as 2018. Leger acquired 51% on 12 March 2024 and the product is now marketed as Cube AI, previously Cube GO; cubehx.com redirects to leger360.com/cube-ai. SCOPE: consumer-neuroscience and neuromarketing analytics — attention, emotion and eye-tracking for customer experience — rather than clinical or BCI neurotech.

name: BeHapbee
note: Year recorded as 2019. Three corrections. The name is a marketing string; the entity is Hapbee Technologies, Inc., incorporated as Elevation Technologies and renamed May 2020. The location is Vancouver, BC, not Seattle — the Seattle link is that the ulRFE technology was invented by EMulate Therapeutics of Seattle and licensed in. And the company has not wound down: it remained listed on TSXV as HAPB, raised CAD 1.507M in June 2025 and reported growing revenue through Q3 2025.

name: Hubly Surgical
note: Year recorded as 2019. The index records San Francisco; it is a Northwestern University student spinout from The Garage accelerator, based in Chicago and Evanston, Illinois. No support for San Francisco was found. Strong fit for the index otherwise: the Hubly Drill is a cranial access drill with an automatic stop for bedside EVD placement, FDA 510(k) cleared May 2023 and in use at Northwestern Medicine.

name: Bio-Signal Technologies
note: Year recorded as 2016, weakly. The about-us page in the index URL is a 404. The live root site carries no founding year, no history and no address, only a US phone number and a WhatsApp contact, and its copy reads as translated boilerplate. Probably a US sales arm for a Chinese neurophysiology-equipment manufacturer rather than an originating developer.

name: Bionen Medical Devices
note: Year recorded as 1989. The URL in the index (www.bionen.it/en.html) is stale: the TLS certificate does not cover the www host and the site has moved to bionen.it/en/. A real operating company in Florence making EEG and EMG needle and surface electrodes, run by the founder daughters Monia and Barbara Nencioni.

name: CerebraCell
note: Year recorded as 2015. Not an independent company but a portfolio venture of Leonhardt Ventures LLC, which spins out single-indication bioelectric companies from a shared patent estate and licenses from InStim. Bioelectric brain stimulation is in scope, but this is a pre-clinical patent-and-press-release operation: its own site says products are not proven safe or effective in controlled studies and are not available for sale.

name: ProtoMe
note: proto-me.com does not resolve. A 2019 figure appears in search summaries but traces only to LinkedIn, Apollo and Parsers.vc. Entity is ProtoMe Technologies Inc, Vancouver BC, brain-health diagnostics, 2-10 employees. Name-collision risk with Protomer Technologies of Pasadena, acquired by Lilly. Likely defunct; a BC Corporate Registry lookup would settle it.

name: BrainGate
note: A multi-institution academic BCI research consortium — Brown, Massachusetts General, Harvard Medical School, Stanford, Baylor, Emory, Rice, UC Davis and the VA Research Service — led clinically by Dr Leigh Hochberg. Three dated events, none a company founding: Cyberkinetics Neurotechnology Systems, a Brown spin-off and now defunct, was formed in 2002; the BrainGate pilot trial began June 2004 with the first implant on 22 June 2004; BrainGate2 began 2008-09. The site footer reads "Copyright 2000-2026 BrainGate" and 2000 must not be used. Note braingate.com is a separate commercial entity and the two should not be merged.

name: Vivid Spectrum Technologies
note: vivid-spectrum.com does not resolve. No institutional, news, registry or accelerator source mentions the company at all; the only trace is a Crunchbase entry describing web-delivered hands-free games for stroke patients recovering hand and arm movement in Ireland. Name searches are polluted by unrelated entities. Not confident the company still operates, or that the Crunchbase entry describes the intended row.

name: CTF
note: The row is CTF MEG (magnetoencephalography), not a generic acronym. Its own about page traces the SQUID technology to 1970, from work under contract to the Canadian Department of National Defence on airborne submarine detection — a lineage date, not a company founding. The corporate chain is CTF Systems Inc of Port Coquitlam, acquired by VSM MedTech around February 2001, later reconstituted; in 2009 CTF acquired the assets of 4D Neuroimaging. Two entities exist today, CTF MEG International Services Limited Partnership and CTF MEG Neuro Innovations, Inc. CB Insights gives 2007, probably the current legal entity. The site now lists Burnaby, BC, so the Coquitlam location is stale.

name: Reminisciences
note: reminisciences.com does not resolve. Aggregators give 2017 for Reminisciences SA of Lausanne and mark it deadpooled. LOCATION: the index says Parys, South Africa; every source says Lausanne, Switzerland. SCOPE: gut-microbiome therapeutics and diagnostics for Alzheimer's (CerebralX, ReminiTest) — a disease overlap, not a technology overlap.

name: Panic Away
note: A self-help information product: a book plus an online course for panic attacks built around a "21-7 Technique", sold direct to consumers by the Irish author Barry McDonagh. No technology, device or software. The current brand vehicle appears to be Dare Response — panicaway.com/about/ is titled "Advisory Board - Dare Response". A search summary dates first publication to 2001, which could not be verified on the live page and would be a book publication date rather than a founding.

name: SOFIA Labs, LLC
note: The index lists an f6s.com aggregator profile as the website, and no real company site exists. Three searches found only aggregator profiles, none carrying a founding year, and Crunchbase marks the company permanently closed. The product was SOFIA's Landscape EXplorer, a cloud SaaS avatar tutor positioning itself against test-prep SaaS and brain trainers such as Lumosity — cognitive-training edtech rather than neurotechnology.

name: iSocial
note: A curriculum, not a company: created by University of Missouri researchers associated with the Thompson Center for Autism and Neurodevelopment to teach social competence to youth with autism, later built into an online virtual world. The commercial vehicle is Nascent Stage Development LLC of Columbia, Missouri, whose own site states no founding year. The only firm date is January 2018, when Missouri announced the licence — a licensing event. The index URL isocl.net redirects to isocialskills.com.

name: NeuroParticle
note: neuroparticle.com redirects to HugeDomains: the domain is parked and for sale. A 2017 figure exists but its only source is medicalsdir.com, an unvetted medical-device directory weaker than Crunchbase and corroborated nowhere, so it is not recorded. Entity is Neuroparticle Corporation, North Bethesda MD, claiming "Neuroparticle therapy" for brain cancer and neurological disease without invasive surgery. Do not confuse with Cellular Nanomed, a different and better-documented magnetoelectric-nanoparticle company co-founded in 2016.

name: Engineering in Medicine & Biology
note: The San Francisco Bay Area chapter of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society — a volunteer chapter of a professional society. Do not assign it a company founding year. Two society dates exist and date different things: 1952 for the IRE Professional Group on Medical Electronics, 1963 for EMBS under its current name. One of the first two EMBS chapters, both approved 7 April 1953, was organised by A.J. Morris of the San Francisco IRE Section, but continuity with the modern chapter is unverified. The index URL redirects to a page that returned no content.

name: Cerebral Vascular Applications
note: A 1999 figure exists on Crunchbase alone and is not recorded. LOCATION: Duluth, Georgia, not Duluth, Minnesota — a portfolio company of The Innovation Factory, a Duluth GA medical device incubator whose own site now fails its TLS chain. SCOPE: minimally invasive left atrial appendage closure to reduce stroke risk in atrial fibrillation, which is a cardiac procedure. No working website and no news since the 2000s. Related patents were filed around 1999, and a patent filing date is not a founding year.

name: URGONight
note: A consumer EEG neurofeedback headband and app for sleep training, not a company. It is made by URGOTECH, a startup created inside the URGO Group, the Dijon wound-care family firm; URGOTECH describes itself as created in 2015. The correct index entry is URGOTECH. Two cautions: the French register aggregator lists URGOTECH under SIREN 532599578, a range typically issued around 2011, which if correct would predate the publicised 2015 date and would in any case be incorporation; and both urgonight.com and urgotech.com failed DNS resolution while their content still appears in search indexes, which is consistent with a wind-down but is not proof.

name: Sleep and Fatigue Research
note: SLEEP AND FATIGUE RESEARCH LTD, company number 09892712, was incorporated 27 November 2015 and DISSOLVED on 26 November 2024. It should be marked defunct. Despite the .org.uk domain it was an ordinary private limited company trading as SAFR, founded by Jason Eden, a former RAF pilot who sat on the Fatigue Risk Management Working Group for large aircraft. The 2015 date is incorporation, not founding, and no separate founding statement exists. SCOPE: fatigue-risk management for commercial drivers using wearables and a bio-mathematical model.

name: Phobious
note: Year recorded as 2013. This row is three renames behind and duplicates two others in the index. Phobious became Psious, rebranded to Amelia Virtual Care in February 2022, and merged with XRHealth of Boston in April 2023. "Psious" and "XRHealth" are both separate rows here. Phobious and Psious are the same company and one of the two rows should not exist; the duplicate audit now catches them because they share a domain.

name: Synergetics USA
note: Year recorded as 1991. Bausch + Lomb announced the acquisition in September 2015 and completed it that October, which is why the row's website resolves to bauschretina.com; the company no longer exists independently. SCOPE: primarily an ophthalmic and vitreoretinal surgical instrument maker. Its only neuro adjacency is a neurosurgery instrument line largely inherited from Valley Forge Scientific's bipolar electrosurgical generators.

name: Mindable Health
note: Year recorded as 2019, disputed against 2018. Every source places Mindable Health GmbH in Berlin, not Stuttgart as the index records. The product is Mindable: Panik & Agoraphobie, a CE-marked prescription DiGA listed in the BfArM directory since April 2021 and reimbursed by German statutory insurance; that 2021 listing is a regulatory milestone and not a founding.

name: EndoSpan
note: Year recorded as 2009, weakly. SCOPE: endovascular stent grafts for aortic arch aneurysms and dissections. This is cardiovascular surgery with no neural component and does not belong in a neurotechnology index. Artivion, Inc. completed its acquisition in May 2026 for up to $375M following April 2026 FDA PMA approval of the NEXUS Aortic Arch System, and endospan.com now carries an Artivion banner.

name: Nanology Labs
note: Year recorded as 2018, weakly. The company is now QurCan Therapeutics Inc.; Crunchbase, PitchBook and Dealroom all redirect the Nanology Labs record to it. A University of Toronto spinout from the Leslie Dan Faculty of Pharmacy. SCOPE: polymer-lipid nanoparticle MRI contrast agents and drug delivery, with brain cancer as one target among several — oncology and imaging chemistry rather than neurotechnology.

name: Calm
note: Year recorded as 2012 and well documented. SCOPE: a consumer meditation and sleep subscription app. No hardware, no neural interface, no neuromodulation, no biosignal acquisition. Its Calm Health arm, launched 2022, is a mental-health content platform. Including it means the index admits any wellness content app that invokes the brain.

name: Brain.fm
note: Year recorded as 2014. The company self-describes its functional music as noninvasive neurostimulation, but there is no device and no neural recording — it is an audio streaming subscription with a neuroscience rationale. Same category as Calm, though Brain.fm at least publishes on the claimed mechanism.

name: Advantis
note: Year recorded as 2016. The company was formerly TomoTECH, so the year may date the earlier name or the rebrand and could not be disambiguated. Advantis Medical Imaging, Athens and Eindhoven, makes Brainance MD for cloud brain MRI analysis, CE marked 2018 and FDA cleared 2021. Its own site has no about page: /about-us/ is a 404.

name: Swap
note: Year recorded as 2014. The website in the index, swap-assist.fr, is superseded by swap-gps.com; the Android package is still fr.swap_assist.swap, confirming one entity. The product is a standalone GPS keychain for Alzheimer's patients with panic button, fall detection and safe-zone alerts. SCOPE: assistive eldercare hardware rather than neurotechnology.

name: ZAPIENS
note: Year recorded as 2014. SCOPE: a conversational corporate knowledge-management and microlearning platform with an AI chatbot, used by Microsoft, IKEA and Vodafone. This is enterprise software, not neurotechnology.

name: Sensae
note: Year recorded as 2020, weakly. The website in the index is wrong: sensae.co now serves an unrelated UK artisanal perfume brand, so the domain has changed hands. The Hub lists the company's site as sensae.com. Beware also a distinct UK company Sensate, a relaxation wearable, which search engines conflate with this one.

name: Mensior
note: Year recorded as 2015, weakly. mensior.com does not resolve and no registry record for Mensior S.r.l. was found, so the company may be defunct. In substance it is genuinely neurotech — an EEG Smart Helmet measuring mental agility for racing drivers, athletes and managers — but Smart Helmet EEG work is also a published Imperial College London line from 2015-2016 and the connection, if any, is unestablished.

name: Ginger Tiger
note: Year recorded as 2013, weakly. SCOPE: special-needs educational software — a library of 350+ learning games for people with learning disabilities, autism and sensory impairments — with no EEG, BCI or neural interface. Distributed in North America via a partnership with Ehave. Note a near-miss: the NoCamels article surfacing on Israeli braintech rehab searches is about Intendu, founded 2012, a different company.

name: Stroke Medical
note: Year recorded as 2016. The row name is a nickname derived from the domain and is not the company's name. strokemedical.com is the corporate site of Shanghai HeartCare Medical Technology Corporation Limited, also rendered Shanghai Xinwei Medical Technology, listed on the Hong Kong exchange as 6609.HK since its 2021 IPO and making neuro-interventional devices for ischaemic and haemorrhagic stroke. The HKEX prospectus of 20 August 2021 would give a filing-grade founding date.

name: Nextstem
note: Year recorded as 2020. The name in the index is wrong: the company is Nexstem, one t, matching nexstem.ai. Non-invasive BCI with the Instinct headset and developer stack; raised $3.5M in November 2024 co-led by Info Edge Ventures, Zupee and Smile Group. LOCATION: Inc42 and other outlets place it in Bengaluru while the index says Gurugram; unresolved.

name: SpinTech Imaging
note: Year recorded as 2017. Now trades as SpinTech MRI, headquartered in Bingham Farms, Michigan. Acquired MR Innovations in February 2021 and has a development partnership with Canon Medical Systems USA. Squarely in scope: STAGE is a quantitative MRI acquisition and post-processing platform for brain imaging in stroke, TBI, Parkinson's, MS and dementia.

name: EyeWire
note: A citizen-science game for reconstructing retinal neurons, run out of Sebastian Seung's lab at MIT and then Princeton, with Amy Robinson Sterling as executive director and NIH grant UH2 CA203710 behind it. It launched 10 December 2012, which is a product launch and not a founding. No distinct commercial entity was found. Note that "Eyewire" was also an unrelated stock-photography brand acquired by Getty Images.

name: Pressao Medical
note: Aggregators give 2018, but the only verifiable fact behind it is an Adventus Ventures seed round dated 9 May 2018, which is a funding date. California records show the company was filed there on 20 August 2021 and formed in Delaware, but a California filing for a Delaware corporation is a foreign qualification, not a founding; the Delaware date is unknown. It was already announcing a CEO hire and Series A in January 2019, so it existed by 2018 at the latest. Genuinely in scope: BP-ADJUST is a wrist-worn neuromodulation device targeting peripheral nerves for uncontrolled hypertension.

name: WizeCare
note: The company's own about page has no founding statement; its only year is a copyright line, which was refused. Aggregators split between 2012 and 2015 with no primary source for either, and the tie could not be broken: the Calcalist article that might have settled it is on a host that no longer resolves. The likely cause of the split is that the company was formerly VideoTherapy, so one year belongs to VideoTherapy and the other to the WizeCare relaunch. Which is which is unknown.

name: Mosaikx
note: The index says Dubai; the company's own press release puts it in Los Angeles, founders Sina Torabi and Mahbod Azadian. Nothing supports Dubai beyond an F6S listicle. The domain has also changed hands or pivoted: mosaikx.com now serves a Los Angeles marketing and automation agency with no neurotech content. The neurotech entry presumably derives from Hipo, a wearable caregiver device for Alzheimer's patients pitched in 2018. Aggregators say 2014; a 2018 release says only that the company won a Hong Kong IoT contest in 2016, shortly after starting — a contest date, not a founding.

name: Excep Apps
note: No source, primary or aggregator, states a founding year. The company did exist: there is a Crunchbase profile, a MobiHealthNews tag, and a reported seed from Iron Yard Ventures, the accelerator arm of The Iron Yard. LOCATION: the index records none, but sources place it in Spartanburg, South Carolina. Iron Yard Ventures wound down around 2017, so the company may be defunct. SCOPE: mobile apps for people with special needs, starting with children with autism — assistive software, not neurotechnology.

name: EyeMove
note: The index records an f6s.com profile in place of a website, and eyemove.online does not resolve. The company is not purely an F6S phantom — there are eyemove.ru social presences and a CEO named Mikhail Yanchikov — but the only year available, 2016 from Tracxn, has no primary corroboration. A Russian EGRUL registry lookup would settle it.

name: Vita Beans Neural Solutions
note: Incorporated 23 December 2008 per the Indian MCA registry, CIN U72900KA2008PTC048680, which embeds KA2008 — an incorporation date, not a founding, so no year is recorded here. SCOPE: the business at vitabeans.com is education technology — learning and assessment, virtual classrooms, student information management, game-based learning. "Neural Solutions" comes from an origin story about building a brain-like AI agent, not from neurotechnology. An edtech company misfiled on the strength of its name.

name: SAM App
note: A university app, not a company: Self-help for Anxiety Management, developed by an interdisciplinary team at UWE Bristol with peer-reviewed publications behind it, launched in the app stores in July 2013 — a product launch. UWE now licenses it to Mind Garden Technology CIC, a Bristol community interest company that operates it on the university's behalf; that entity's incorporation year was not established and it is a licensee rather than the originator. The app now also lives at mindgarden-tech.co.uk.

name: Mental Waves® for happiness
note: A personal brand, as the registered-trademark symbol in the row name hints: the trading name of Alex Michel, a Montpellier composer of therapeutic music who describes himself as founder of Mental Waves. No SIRET, no legal entity registration and no incorporation record were found; the string "Mind Response" in the site's copyright line may be the actual entity but nothing corroborates it. The site offers only two date signals, both excluded by the rules: a copyright range of 2011-2026 and the phrase "depuis plus de 15 ans". SCOPE: immersive sound experiences and binaural audio — the brainwave vocabulary is thematic, with no measurement, device or interface.

name: Fondly
note: The index stores no website and no location, and no company of this name could be found anywhere in the neurotech, mental-health, EEG or dementia space. What exists under the name is a scatter of unrelated consumer apps: a Fondly dementia family app at fondly.co whose Facebook page was last active around 2015, a Fondly Memory Journal on the App Store, a couples game by a different developer, and a cards app. Almost certainly different products sharing a common word. No basis to pick one, and a candidate for deletion unless a source exists for what the row was meant to be.

name: Litha Group
note: LITHA GROUP LTD, company number 14246262, incorporated 20 July 2022 and DISSOLVED 10 September 2024. The incorporation date is the only date on record and must not be read as a founding. litha.org does not resolve. It was renamed from HUMAN LTD within nine days of incorporation. SCOPE: its SIC code is generic software development and the only description found is conversational AI for human-computer interaction, which is not neurotechnology. Identification is reasonably but not fully certain: the Warwickshire registered office near Bidford-on-Avon matches the index, though Companies House now shows Leicester.

name: CONSTRUKTS, Inc.
note: Aggregators say 2008; the company site carries a copyright range of 2014-2025, which was refused as evidence. Three primary sources — the homepage, the about and team page, and the founder's own site — state no founding year, and the NSF grant release omits it. LOCATION: the index says Chicago; the NSF release datelines Wilmington NC and aggregators list Raleigh, with no Chicago connection found. SCOPE: a digital-twin STEM learning platform of IoT smart blocks with AI model analysis and AR — edtech with no neural sensing. Founder Pamela L. Jennings PhD.

name: Explorer Research
note: Year recorded as 2002. Savanta, part of Next 15 Group plc, acquired the company in December 2023; it still trades under the Explorer Research brand. SCOPE: consumer neuromarketing and shopper research using eye tracking and implicit response, rather than clinical neurotechnology.

name: Lifelines Neurodiagnostic Systems
note: Year recorded as 2001. The index says Troy, Illinois, which is a legacy or secondary site; the HQ is Louisville, Kentucky, with London and Dublin offices. Corporate history matters here: it acquired Lifelines Ltd of the UK in 2017 and Incereb of Ireland in 2018, and in 2019 a joint venture merged four companies into Lifelines Neuro Company under SIDIS Global. Both Incereb and Eegapps Medical are separate rows in this index, so three rows describe one group.

name: ADmit Therapeutics
note: Year recorded as 2017, well sourced to the parent institute. But this is an in-vitro diagnostics company: MAP-AD is an epigenetic blood test with an algorithm stratifying mild cognitive impairment patients by risk of progression. Neither a device nor software acting on the nervous system, and not a drug developer either despite the name.

name: Marigold Health
note: Year recorded as 2016, weakly. The company has renamed twice: Beacon, a Johns Hopkins student project in the 2016-17 Social Innovation Lab cohort, then Sunrise Health, then Marigold Health. CB Insights still files it under the sunrise-health slug. SCOPE: text-based peer support for behavioural health and substance use disorder with NLP triage — mental-health software with no neural signal.

name: aidoc
note: Year recorded as 2016 from the company's own about page. SCOPE: a general clinical-AI and radiology triage platform spanning radiology, cardiology, neurovascular and vascular, with 18+ FDA-cleared algorithms; by its own account it covers 75% of a facility's patient population. It belongs in a neurotechnology index only through its intracranial-haemorrhage and large-vessel-occlusion products. It is also very large — 1,600+ medical centres, over $500M raised, pre-IPO — so it may distort a startup-oriented index.

name: BrainVoyager
note: Year recorded as 2000. BrainVoyager is a software package; the company is Brain Innovation B.V. of Maastricht, founded by Rainer Goebel, who is also Professor of Cognitive Neuroscience at Maastricht University. The row should be renamed to Brain Innovation B.V. with BrainVoyager as its product. Product line: BrainVoyager, Turbo-BrainVoyager for real-time fMRI neurofeedback, and PowerMAGView for TMS neuronavigation.

name: Mundo Pato
note: Year recorded as 2010, on aggregators alone. mundopato.com resolves to UnitusTI, Unitus Therapy Intelligence, operated by Mundo Pato Inc of Portland — so the row is named after the holding company while the product carries a different brand. SCOPE: a HIPAA and GDPR compliant SaaS for data collection and curriculum in ABA therapy, autism and special-needs education. Practice-management software, not neurotechnology.

name: DeepMind
note: Year recorded as 2010, disputed against 2011. SCOPE: a general artificial-intelligence research lab — game-playing agents, AlphaFold, language models. It draws inspiration from neuroscience, which is almost certainly why it was swept into this index, but neuroscience-inspired AI is not neurotechnology and it builds nothing that interfaces with the nervous system. Acquired by Google in 2014, merged with Google Brain in 2023, now Google DeepMind under Alphabet. The recorded URL is stale; the site is deepmind.google.

name: Moodpanda
note: Year recorded as 2011, as a launch. SCOPE: a self-reported mood diary and happiness tracker with a peer-support community, where users type a 0-10 score. No sensing, no signal acquisition, no neural component. Founders Ross Larter and Jake Greenwood. The live site still serves classic ASP.NET .aspx pages and the blog is a Tumblr, so it may be dormant.

name: Neurallys
note: Year recorded as 2016. The index says Paris, which reflects only its incubation at the Institut du Cerveau; it was founded within the Caen faculty of medicine and moved its HQ and R&D to Colombelles in Normandy in 2017. neurallys.com refused connection on fetch and may be dead. Genuinely in scope: an implantable intracranial-pressure sensor for hydrocephalus shunt patients.

name: Owl Insights
note: Year recorded as 2011, disputed against 2013. Acquired by NeuroFlow in June 2024 and no longer independent; owlinsights.com refused connection and appears dead post-acquisition. The legal entity is Mental Health Data Services, Inc., dba Owl Insights, later branded Owl Health. LOCATION: originally Kirkland WA, later Portland Oregon; the index says Seattle. SCOPE: measurement-based behavioural-health SaaS, not neurotechnology.

name: EyeControl
note: Year recorded as 2016. The registered entity appears to be Eyefree Assisting Communication Ltd, listed that way in an EU Commission Futurium entry; the row name is the product brand. A screenless wearable eye-tracking communication device for ALS and locked-in patients, later extended as EyeControl-Pro for ICU delirium. Harvard Business School case 820078 would be a good corroborating source for the year.

name: Mightier
note: Year recorded as 2014, disputed against 2016. Mightier is the product: a biofeedback video-game system teaching emotional regulation to children, using a heart-rate wearable to gate gameplay. The company is Neuromotion Inc, dba Neuromotion Labs, Boston, founders Craig Lund and Jason Kahn — a genuine Boston Children's Hospital and Harvard Medical School spinout whose underlying research programme began around 2009. The product was released in 2017 and renamed Mightier in 2018; neither is a founding date.

name: Invention Labs
note: Year recorded as 2007. The row is named after the parent but the live brand is Avaz Inc: inventionlabs.in is legacy and its about page returns a 500, while the operating site is avazapp.com. Legal name Invention Labs Engineering Products Private Limited, an IIT Madras incubated company; founder Ajit Narayanan. Avaz is an AAC app for children with speech disability and autism.

name: Encope
note: Two searches, Danish CVR and neurotech-startup angles, returned zero mentions of any company named Encope in Copenhagen or anywhere. The index website field is the literal placeholder "https://Web", so no site was ever recorded. Likely a data-entry artefact, a misspelling, or a defunct entity that left no web footprint.

name: HomeoLux
note: homeolux.com now redirects to beacon40.com: the company rebranded to BEACON40, with Homeolux, Inc. still the legal entity. Founder and chairman Terry Moore built it after his wife's Alzheimer's diagnosis, on the MIT 40Hz gamma work. A 2018 year circulates on CB Insights alone, with no primary source, so none is recorded. SCOPE: the site explicitly markets a "non-wearable, non-medical device" wellness lamp. Do not confuse with Cognito Therapeutics of Boston, a different gamma-stimulation company.

name: Nerve renew
note: Not a company on any axis. Nerve Renew is a dietary supplement — a B-vitamin, R-alpha-lipoic-acid and benfotiamine blend for peripheral neuropathy, listed in the NIH Dietary Supplement Label Database. The URL in the index, fitbitehealth.com, is an affiliate review site that self-describes as "Guide Health Pills Verified Customer Reviews" and is not the publisher. The actual seller is Neuropathy Treatment Group, dba Life Renew, of Boise, Idaho, not Princeton. NutraIngredients-USA reported the maker dropped advertising claims in 2021 after a Council for Responsible Nutrition challenge.

name: Lief Therapeutics
note: One source gives 2012; others state only that Rohan Dixit "has been CEO of Lief since 2015", which establishes existence by 2015 and not a founding. Neither traces to a primary source. The gap is wide enough that one is probably a different milestone. Real and active: an HRV-biofeedback wearable patch out of Harvard and Stanford meditation research, now selling Lief Rx as a prescription device. The primary site has moved to lief.ai; getlief.com still takes orders.

name: Terenz
note: terenz.ai does not resolve. The entity is real — 주식회사 테렌즈, a Busan AI medical-imaging startup co-founded by Dr James Sathya of Inje University and Kim Jong-chul, named best innovative startup at BOUNCE 2019, so it existed by 2019 — but no source states a founding year. A possible successor entity, Terenz Labs, also appears in Busan sources. SCOPE: general AI medical imaging; a Parkinson's screening angle is the only neuro tie.

name: mindreach
note: mindreach.org issues a 307 redirect to GoDaddy's for-sale parking page. No entity of this name in Lisbon surfaced in search, and it could not be established whether it was a company, a nonprofit or a project. Looks like a stale entry harvested from a domain that has since lapsed.

name: Farol VR
note: farolvr.com.br does not resolve. Two searches in Portuguese and English returned nothing for Farol VR or FarolVR beyond unrelated Brazilian VR firms. The entity could not be confirmed to exist, let alone to be neurotech. A Brazilian CNPJ lookup would be the next step.

name: Cognition Medical
note: The company site says only "Alex founded Cognition Medical while completing his PhD" and states no year anywhere. Crunchbase shows 2012, which is hard to reconcile with a 2019 interview in which CEO Alex Turjman said he started the company "a couple years back" and with first patent applications filed in December 2015; no arithmetic was done on that phrase. Genuinely in scope: interventional neurovascular clot-retrieval devices for acute ischaemic stroke, out of Prof. Elazer Edelman's lab at MIT and Brigham and Women's. The Massachusetts corporate registry would settle it.

name: Neurorobotics Research Laboratory
note: A university research laboratory at Berliner Hochschule fuer Technik, Fachbereich VII, led by Prof. Dr Manfred Hild, professor for Digital Systems there since 2014 — a biography date that must not be used as a founding year. Research is on morphologies and distributed neural systems for autonomous robots: neural-network-inspired robotics, not neurotechnology acting on a nervous system.

name: DataNovo, Inc.
note: A patent and legal analytics company: AI-driven prior art search across 80M+ references, validity scoring, litigation outcome forecasting. Clients are patent offices, law firms and IP investors. The only plausible reason it landed in a neurotech index is the phrase "neural network" in its AI marketing. Its own site states no founding year; Tracxn gives 2015, aggregator-only, so none is recorded. Its stored description is also one of the seventeen corrupted ones, reading "USA - SF/Bay Area".

name: Roshi
note: ROSHI is a product line — ROSHI, pROSHI, ROSHIWave EEG neurofeedback and brainwave-entrainment devices — created by Chuck Davis, listed as CEO of "ROSHI Corporation". The only date found, 1988, is when the underlying software and hardware were developed, not a company founding. roshi.com sits behind a WAF with a mismatched certificate and would not load. The Pasadena location is weak and possibly mis-derived: Davis worked at JPL there decades ago and a separate Pasadena neurofeedback clinic uses the device. Recent marketing comes from mindmachines.com, a reseller.

name: CerQana
note: An Android launcher that simplifies a smartphone to four large pictogram buttons with GPS location, sold for elderly people and people with autism or Down syndrome so caregivers can check on them. No sensing, stimulation or neural signal. The only dates are relative and mutually inconsistent — "todo comenzo hace un ano" in February 2016 against an idea emerging in February 2014 — and no arithmetic was done on either. One 2022 source says CerQana no longer exists; cerqana.com returned HTTP 429 on three attempts.

name: BrainFul
note: No founding year: the site carries only a copyright line and marketing copy, with no about page. Real and neurotech-adjacent — Brainful Inc., founder and CEO Christopher deCharms, the same deCharms behind Omneuron, which is a different entity and must not be merged. LOCATION: the index says San Francisco but the live site's contact address is in Vega Baja, Puerto Rico. Aggregator years around 2014 could not be verified.

name: My Sensory Locations
note: Broken on three axes. mysensorytools.com redirects to a HugeDomains for-sale page. The row name does not match the domain and reads as a mangled nickname. And the only live "My Sensory Tools" findable is a fidget and sensory toy shop in Lebanon, Ohio — not Doylestown, Pennsylvania, and a toy retailer rather than a neurotechnology company.

name: Imexco
note: imexco.com resolves to IMEXCO General Ltd fronting an antiques online catalogue, with no about page and no founding year. The neurotech classification is nonetheless defensible: IMEXCO General Ltd of Ramat HaSharon is a project-oriented R&D house founded by Giora Ram, working on medical diagnostic equipment in neurology, cardiology and pain monitoring including a chronic-pain detection application. The same domain also hosts Ram's antiques business, which makes it look like a personal holding domain. Subdomains nuke.imexco.com and edu.imexco.com do not resolve. The Start-Up Nation Central page returns 403 and is the best remaining lead.

name: PathMaker Neurosystems
note: The about page states no founding year; its only date marker is a copyright range beginning 2015, which is not usable. Crunchbase gives 2015 alone, weakly echoed by that range, and no primary source corroborates it. Real and active: clinical-stage non-invasive trans-spinal direct current stimulation, lead device MyoRegulator for spasticity, plus an ALS programme. CEO Nader Yaghoubi; scientific founder Dr Zaghloul Ahmed of CUNY Staten Island. Dates that are NOT foundings: first MyoRegulator trial with the Feinstein Institute in April 2016, and a French-American Business Award in 2018.

name: Aural Analytics
note: Year recorded as 2015, aggregator-only. Acquired by Linus Health in March 2024 and no longer independent. An Arizona State University spinout commercialising speech analytics for neurological disease; the index location is correct.

name: Phosphoenix
note: Year recorded as 2019. The index says Delft; the company is a spin-off of the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience in Amsterdam, and other sources place it there. Delft may be an operational address but Amsterdam is the origin. Genuinely in scope: a cortical visual prosthesis.

name: BioAxone Therapeutic
note: Year recorded as 2000. SCOPE: a drug developer, not device or software neurotech — Cethrin/BA-210 is a Rho antagonist for acute spinal cord injury. bioaxone.com refuses connections and the Canadian entity is effectively defunct; founder Lisa McKerracher acquired the assets and formed BioAxone BioSciences, Inc. in Cambridge, Massachusetts around 2011. The two must not be merged.

name: Reha Technology
note: Year recorded as 2011, and it is an incorporation date rather than a founding. Bankruptcy proceedings were opened on 31 July 2025 by the district court president of Olten-Goesgen; the Swiss registry name is now "Reha Technology AG in Liquidation". The website was still serving when checked, so the site being up is not evidence the company is.

name: Medibrane
note: Year recorded as 2015, well sourced. SCOPE: polymeric covers and coatings for nitinol stent scaffolds, made by sutureless lamination, dipping and spraying. The "brane" is membrane, not brain. This is a name-based false inclusion rather than ordinary scope drift — the same shape as DataNovo and Vita Beans Neural Solutions.

name: Nervex Neurotechnologies
note: Year recorded as 2021. The URL in the index, nervexneurotech.com, is not the live site; the company operates at nervex.tech. A University of Toronto spinout whose original product ANIMO is a genuine adaptive neural implant for epilepsy, but the current site foregrounds NXVET, an AI stethoscope attachment measuring temperature, pulse and respiration in animals — a pivot toward veterinary vital signs worth a scope re-check.

name: BioBeat
note: Year recorded as 2016. The correct styling is Biobeat, one word. SCOPE: wearable remote patient monitoring — a disposable chest patch and wrist monitor covering around thirteen parameters including cuffless PPG blood pressure, pulse, respiratory rate, SpO2 and ECG, FDA-cleared and CE marked. Cardiovascular and vital-signs monitoring with nothing acting on the nervous system. bio-beat.com/about returns 404.

name: Juno Biomedical Inc.
note: Year recorded as 2014. The company release datelines Mountain View, California, not the San Jose the index records. Regenerative and bioelectric therapy for stroke and TBI. No evidence of activity after about 2017, so operating status is unknown.

name: Axorus
note: Year recorded as 2019, disputed against 2018. The company states it "definitively abandoned its neuro-electronic implant technology in 2021, and its invasive photoacoustic implants in early 2025", and is now positioned as a non-invasive photoacoustic contact lens for dry AMD. That pushes it toward ophthalmic devices and away from neurotechnology.

name: Neuroenhancement Lab
note: Year recorded as 2017, aggregator-only. Renamed to NeuroLight, Inc. on 25 October 2022, moving from transcranial electrical stimulation to light and sound photobiomodulation; the product is the NeuroMask, first targeting insomnia. neuroenhancementlab.com returns HTTP 526 and the live site is neurolight.co. Despite the name it is a company, not a clinic, so it stays in scope.

name: Mira Rehab
note: Year recorded as 2012, aggregator-only. Both mirarehab.com and www.mirarehab.com fail DNS resolution entirely, not merely 404. Software turning physiotherapy and cognitive exercises into depth-sensor-tracked video games, with UK and Romania locations; current operating status unclear.

name: Ybrain
note: Year recorded as 2013 from the company's own history page, the best-sourced result in its batch. The index spells the location "Seongman"; it is Seongnam-si, Gyeonggi-do, at 54 Changeop-ro, Sujeong-gu.

name: NextMind
note: Year recorded as 2017. Acquired by Snap Inc., announced 23 March 2022. It did not wind down: the roughly twenty-person team stayed in Paris and was folded into Snap Lab, Snap's hardware R&D group, while the consumer Dev Kit headband was discontinued and next-mind.com should be treated as defunct. The spin-out parent is Ecole Normale Superieure, not the Institut de la Vision.

name: Rithmi
note: Year recorded as 2016. SCOPE: atrial fibrillation detection through a wearable and the FlashCheck app, which uses the phone camera and flash for photoplethysmography. Marketed as a "pulsera antiictus", stroke prevention — but AF is a cardiac arrhythmia and this is cardiovascular prevention, not neurotechnology. LOCATION: born in Castellon and later based in Valencia.

name: Sands Research
note: Year recorded as 2008 from the company's own profile. SCOPE: neuromarketing — EEG-based advertising research, best known for an annual Super Bowl ad neuro ranking — rather than clinical or device neurotech. Has since merged with Neurons Inc., a Danish neuromarketing firm, so the standalone entity may no longer be independent.

name: See-Mode Technologies
note: Year recorded as 2017. Acquired by RadNet, announced June 2025, and folded into its AI arm DeepHealth; see-mode.com now redirects to deephealth.com and the standalone company no longer exists under that name. It operated across Singapore and Melbourne, so the Singapore location is defensible but incomplete.

name: EMVision Medical
note: Year recorded as 2017. A University of Queensland spin-out making a portable microwave brain scanner for stroke, listed on the ASX. The index says Brisbane, which tracks the UQ origin, but the registered corporate office is Sydney. Note for anyone re-checking: this listed via a conventional IPO trading from 13 December 2018, not a reverse takeover, so that 2018 date is a listing and not a second founding.

name: Neuvana Life
note: Year recorded as 2014, against the company's own claim of 2016. The entity chain is Nervana LLC to Neuvana; 2016 is the rebrand. The Xen vagus-nerve-stimulation earbud is still sold through a live storefront with HSA and FSA eligibility. It is marketed as a consumer wellness device rather than a regulated medical device.

name: Medtronic Vascular
note: A subsidiary of Medtronic plc, not an independent company, and three years must not be blended: 1949 is Medtronic's founding, 1991 is Arterial Vascular Engineering of Santa Rosa whose entity and site became Medtronic Vascular, and 1998-99 is the acquisition. The name itself is post-acquisition branding, so no year is recorded here. SCOPE: coronary, peripheral and aortic stents. It touches neurovascular indications, but that is vascular access to the brain rather than neurotechnology; Medtronic's neuro business is a separate division. The Santa Rosa site is being closed, with departures from spring 2027. NOTE: this index holds three Medtronic rows, and the one simply called "Medtronic" carries medina-medical.com, the domain of a neurovascular company Medtronic acquired in 2015.

name: Upcard
note: upcard.io fails TLS negotiation and one search result flagged the domain as possibly for sale. Serious name collision: UPCARD SAS is a Colombian fintech, and there is an unrelated UpCard digital business card app. The entity that would plausibly match Uppsala is an accessibility platform of digital picture cards for children with autism and ADHD, but the Uppsala Innovation Centre portfolio does not list it and no legal name or year could be confirmed. Verify the company exists before assigning anything.

name: Artificial Cognition, Inc.
note: artificialcognition.ai refuses connections and Crunchbase obfuscates the founded date for this profile. Consistently reported as a New York company of roughly one to ten people, founder and CEO Robert Polkowski, building AI wearables to mitigate cognitive impairment including dementia — a legitimate adjacency if it still operates, which could not be confirmed. Searches are pulled toward the unrelated and far larger Cognition AI, founded 2023; that year must not leak in.

name: Tickments
note: Incorporated 16 May 2017 per Corporations Canada, ID 10237817, Ottawa, and DISSOLVED 27 September 2024. The site is a stale shell for a beta school app and carries a 2017 footer, which was not used — the register gives the same year independently. SCOPE: no discernible nervous-system connection at all. This reads as an education and scheduling app and nothing found explains why it is in a neurotechnology index.

name: Idox Health
note: A brand and division of Idox Group plc, and the legal entity behind the name was DISSOLVED on 27 December 2022. Three competing years and no clean answer: 1991 is the incorporation of the entity that later became Idox Health Limited but was then Peter Wright Software; 1999 is given by aggregators for Blithe Computer Systems, the Burton-on-Trent EPR business that is the real operational ancestor, which contradicts the register's 1997 rename; and 2011 is a marketing claim about market entry. SCOPE: health records and case-management software. Managing a stroke or dementia caseload is not neurotechnology.

name: Handl Medical
note: A real neuromodulation venture — a drug-free portable device stimulating peripheral nerves in the palm to treat migraine, genuinely in scope — but no source states a founding year. It appears in the QB3 and Rosenman Institute portfolios dated 22 June 2018, which is a portfolio listing and was not used. Both accelerator pages are now broken. The index's "https://N/A" is accurate; no live site exists. Beware the name collision with Handl Therapeutics of Leuven, a gene-therapy company acquired by UCB in November 2020, which dominates search results.

name: Centro de Psicología Álava Reyes
note: A private psychology clinic in Madrid directed by Maria Jesus Alava Reyes, staffed by psychologists, psychiatrists, neuropsychologists and speech therapists, offering talk therapy. Employing neuropsychologists is not neurotechnology; it builds and sells no device, software or measurement technology. Its own site gives only a decade — "desde su creacion en los anos ochenta" — and the "more than 40 years" figure on directory sites is a rolling marketing claim, so no year is recorded and no arithmetic was done.

name: MieronVR
note: The company's own About page states no year. Tracxn says 2015, founded by Josh Dubon; the Las Vegas Review-Journal in January 2020 says he and co-founder Jessica Maslin got the founding phone call "two and a half years ago" and a April 2020 piece says "around three years ago", both pointing at about 2017 — relative phrases that were not converted. The 2015 against 2017 gap is too wide to paper over. Real and in scope: VR neurotherapy for spinal cord and traumatic brain injury rehabilitation. The legal entity is Mieron, Inc. and two domains are live.

name: Suva Technologies Inc.
note: suva.ca redirects to a domain-parking sale page. A real Victoria BC mobile-EEG software house founded by Dr Nolan Beise, whose product Aspire launched at CES in January 2019 — genuinely neurotech — but the only year available, 2017, traces to aggregator data and could not be confirmed on any page. Beise has since founded Circl, and SUVA appears defunct or dormant. Do not confuse with suva-tech.com, an unrelated Uruguayan bat-acoustics company.

name: Ampere Medical
note: A real, live Hong Kong company — Ampere Medical Limited, Kowloon, directed by Dr Frank Zhu — but a DISTRIBUTOR and training provider rather than a technology developer. It resells Nexstim's navigated TMS and Soterix Medical's transcranial electrical stimulation in Hong Kong and China and sells paid nTMS courses. No page states a founding year and the only date is a 2025 copyright footer, which was not used. The earliest hard datapoint is a 2018 Nexstim distribution agreement, a commercial milestone that postdates the company.

name: Carevium
note: carevium.com redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale page and the company appears defunct. Aggregators give 2014; no primary source exists, so no year is recorded. SCOPE: web-based resident-care management software for assisted and senior living — CRM, eMAR, billing, census reporting. Its only neuro link is that some customers run memory-care units; it neither measures nor acts on the nervous system.

name: NewTouch Digital
note: newtouchdigital.com redirects to neurorpm.com: the company now trades as NeuroRPM Inc., legal entity historically New Touch Digital, Inc. Founders Atila Omer, Jonathan Pomeraniec and Alexander Ksendzovsky. Clearly in scope — FDA-cleared AI monitoring of Parkinson's motor symptoms on Apple Watch. Aggregators give 2017 but the company's own site and team page state no year and carry only a 2023-2026 copyright, so none is recorded.

name: Sidekicks
note: Sidekicks is an app; the company is The Affinity Project, founded by the Pulitzer-winning journalist Ron Suskind in Cambridge, Massachusetts, inspired by his book and documentary Life, Animated. The app is an avatar-based communication aid for autistic children, built with input from a co-inventor of Siri. sidekicks.com returns 503 on repeated attempts and the company's own site is the-affinity-project.com. Tracxn gives 2015, aggregator-only, so no year is recorded. Beware collisions with a Boston home-improvement startup and a UK Sidekicks Services Ltd.

name: LocateMotion
note: A subsidiary of MarkiTech founded by Nauman Jaffar, now operating mainly as SenSights.AI; locatemotion.com would not load, so the indexed URL is likely stale. LOCATION: Toronto, which the index records as unknown. Aggregators give 2017 with no primary source, so no year is recorded. SCOPE: IoT caregiver wearables and remote patient monitoring for seniors including people with dementia — location tracking and vital-signs monitoring, where the dementia angle is a target market rather than a mechanism.

name: Marmot Labs
note: Year recorded as 2017, an incorporation date. DISSOLVED 15 February 2022 and marmotlabs.io no longer resolves; the SETsquared accelerator page for it now 404s. The business was VR plus biofeedback software for anxiety and phobia therapy, with generic software-development SIC codes. LOCATION: the registered office was Watford, not London.

name: RemindMe
note: Year recorded as 2012. RemindMeCare, also written ReMindMe or ReMeLife, is the product; the company is Health-Connected Ltd of the UK, founders reported as Etienne Abrahams and Simon Hooper. Companies House lists a Leeds registered office while the operating base is usually given as London. The product launched around 2016, several years after the incorporation.

name: VRapeutic
note: Year recorded as 2017, weakly. The site now lists 1344 Notting Hill Avenue, Ottawa, Ontario and the entity styles itself VRapeutic Inc.; the index's Alexandria, Egypt is the origin rather than the current base. VR therapy modules for children with ADHD and autism plus wearable bio-sensors for motor training — defensible in a broad reading, but not a brain-interface technology.

name: Twenty Billion Neurons
note: Year recorded as 2015 from the company's own account. SCOPE: video understanding, a 220k-clip labelled human-action dataset, synthetic training data and "common sense" avatars for smart home, fitness and automotive. General-purpose machine learning where "Neurons" is the only neuro connection — the same name-based inclusion pattern as Medibrane and DataNovo. Qualcomm acquired the team in July 2021 and the operating business no longer exists.

name: Interactive Productline
note: Year recorded as 2002 from the Swedish register. RENAMED to Mentalytics AB on the same org.nr, 556633-2036, so it is one legal entity and the founding year carries over. The row is also named after its product, Mindball, which originated as research at the Swedish Interactive Institute in October 2002 with the first game shipping in 2003. The index should carry Mentalytics AB and probably a new website.

name: Q30 Innovations
note: Year recorded as 2012, disputed against 2013. The live site is q30.com, not the indexed q30innovations.com. Two entity names circulate, Q30 Innovations, LLC and Q30 Sports Science, LLC, and a Senate release calls it Norwalk-based rather than Westport. Strongly in scope: the Q-Collar applies light pressure to the jugular veins to reduce brain movement on impact, FDA-cleared 26 February 2021 as the first device of its kind, with a $2.8M USAMRDC contract in October 2022. Neither the clearance nor the September 2021 launch is a founding date.

name: Brainsgate
note: Year recorded as 2000, aggregator-only. brainsgate.com and www.brainsgate.com both fail TLS validation: the certificate presented belongs to stick.tyco.co.il, an unrelated Israeli host, so the domain's hosting appears repointed. The correct styling is BrainsGate. Investors included Medtronic, J&J Development, Boston Scientific, Elron and Pitango; the last notable news is a $14M raise in December 2020, so operating status is worth re-checking.

name: Whale Imaging
note: Year recorded as 1998, aggregator-only and contested against 2009. SCOPE: the G-Arm bi-plane mobile surgical fluoroscopy system and Sigma portable diagnostic ultrasound — general surgical and diagnostic imaging hardware. Its marketing lists neurosurgery alongside orthopaedics, spine and pain management, but the device is not nervous-system-specific and neither measures nor modulates neural activity. This looks like a row included because "neurosurgery" appears in a specialty list.

name: Pocketcoach
note: Year recorded as 2019 from two independent Austrian startup outlets. SCOPE: a text-based CBT chatbot for anxiety and stress, later certified for German statutory insurance reimbursement. No sensor, no signal acquisition, no nervous-system interface. The Crunchbase record resolves under the name Stresscoach, so the company or product may have been renamed.

name: Brain Resource
note: Year recorded as 2000, aggregator-only.
