Founded by Dr Evian Gordon out of the Brain Dynamics Centre at Westmead Hospital and the University of Sydney; it built the first standardised international brain database and listed on the ASX as BRC, now delisted. The platform became MyBrainSolutions and then Total Brain in 2018, and Total Brain has since been acquired by SonderMind. LOCATION: Sydney in origin, not San Francisco. brainresource.com no longer resolves.

name: MitoDys Therapeutics Ltd
note: Year recorded as 2012, an incorporation date. DISSOLVED 21 June 2022; mitodys.com is a leftover. SCOPE: a virtual drug-discovery company repositioning small molecules against mitochondrial dysfunction in Parkinson's and rare neurodegenerative disease — therapeutics rather than a device or software. LOCATION: the registered office was Chipping Norton, Oxfordshire, not Oxford.

name: Mindset Health
note: Year recorded as 2018 from Y Combinator. SCOPE: hypnotherapy delivered by app — Nerva for IBS, Evia for menopausal hot flushes, Finito for smoking cessation. Gut-brain-axis behavioural therapeutics with no sensing, stimulation or neural interface. The row is also named after an app: the indexed themindsetapp.com is a legacy product domain and the corporate site is mindsethealth.com.

name: BrainMARC
note: Year recorded as 2013. LOCATION: an Israeli company headquartered in Yokneam, described by NoCamels as American-Israeli; the index's Hoboken is wrong. brainmarc.com does not resolve at all, which suggests the company may no longer be operating. Genuinely in scope: EEG headsets producing a Brain Engagement Index measuring attention during cognitive therapy.

name: Joyable
note: Year recorded as 2013. Acquired by AbleTo on 6 March 2019 for an undisclosed eight-figure sum, with co-founder Peter Shalek becoming AbleTo's chief product officer; AbleTo was itself later acquired by UnitedHealth/Optum, so the company no longer exists independently. SCOPE: online CBT with human coaching — behavioural health software with no neural sensing or stimulation.

name: Teledyne Scientific & Imaging
note: Year recorded as 1962, for the R&D institution rather than the named entity. A wholly-owned subsidiary of Teledyne Technologies, not an independent company, sharing the Thousand Oaks complex with the parent's corporate headquarters. SCOPE: a general corporate R&D house — infrared and visible imaging sensors, advanced ceramics, liquid-crystal displays, high-speed electronics. Not a neurotechnology company; any neuro connection is incidental to its sensors turning up in scientific instrumentation broadly.

name: Proneuron Biotechnologies
note: Year recorded as 1996, aggregator-only. SCOPE: a cell-therapy developer, not a device company — ProCord was autologous activated macrophages injected into the injured spinal cord, licensed from Yeda, scientific founder Prof. Michal Schwartz of the Weizmann Institute. FDA orphan drug designation September 2004 and Phase II with Craig Hospital; the trial was reportedly halted and there has been no activity in roughly two decades. LOCATION: an Israeli company in Ness Ziona with a US shell for the trials; New York is wrong. proneuron.com redirects to a sale page.

name: Eodyne Systems
note: Year recorded as 2014. CONFIRMED DUPLICATE of the row simply called "Eodyne": eodyne.com redirects to eodynesystems.com and both rows are Barcelona. The two should be merged. A spin-off of the SPECS group at Universitat Pompeu Fabra and ICREA, commercialising the Rehabilitation Gaming System invented by Paul F.M.J. Verschure — VR-based neurorehabilitation for stroke, validated in clinical trials and deployed in hospitals. Legitimately neurotech.

name: The Rowing Team
note: The parent entity of Blue Ocean Brain, a workplace microlearning app marketed as "grounded in the latest neuroscience" and launched September 2012 — corporate e-learning content with neuroscience branding, not neurotechnology. A Virginia SCC record gives LLC formation on 14 September 2010, an incorporation date recorded here rather than as a founding; the source is a city-data mirror rather than the register itself. Crunchbase lists the entity as permanently closed while the business appears to have continued under the Blue Ocean Brain name.

name: System2 Neurotechnology
note: system2neurotech.com returns HTTP 404. Genuinely neurotech in intent — a multimodal wearable fNIRS and EEG passive BCI for neuroergonomics, co-founder named as Sam Mackenzie — but the only surviving traces are aggregator profiles, a BCI wiki entry and a dormant social account. Apollo gives 2020, which was not treated as sufficient. LOCATION: Toronto, which the index records as unknown. Probably a stalled or defunct micro-startup.

name: Avail Support
note: The Irish Times reports Avail was launched in 2017 with Enterprise Ireland backing, founded by Lisa Marie Clinton — "launched" phrasing rather than a founding statement, so no year is recorded; the Irish CRO register would settle it. ACQUIRED in 2021 by the US firm CentralReach and now operating as Avail by CentralReach; the .ie domain in the index is superseded by availsupport.com. SCOPE: video-based step-by-step learning plans for neurodiverse users — disability support software rather than nervous-system technology.

name: LARKR
note: No founding year exists in any source; what exists are launch dates — press coverage April 2017, App Store 16 October 2017, reSET accelerator January 2018 — all of which were refused. Larkr Inc. was founded by Shawn Kernes, formerly StubHub CTO, with Christianne Kernes. Crunchbase lists it closed and larkr.com appears defunct, the only live presence an unmaintained staging site. SCOPE: a teletherapy marketplace connecting users to human therapists by video, with no neurotechnology of any kind.

name: Pufferfish Software
note: pufferfishapps.com now resolves only as ww38.pufferfishapps.com, the classic parked or resold pattern, and even that fails DNS. Not a company in the ordinary sense: a one-person iPad app shop started by Megan Holstein in Columbus, Ohio at age fifteen to build autism communication apps for her brother, five apps in total. The founder's own page is a 404. Aggregators split 2011 against 2012 with no primary source for either. LOCATION: Columbus, Ohio, which the index records as unknown.

name: Grace App
note: A product with no company behind it that could be established. Grace App is an AAC picture-exchange app conceived by Lisa Domican, a mother of two autistic children in Wicklow, and built with developer Steven Troughton-Smith; it is named after her daughter. A trading name "Grace App Communications" appears in the World Summit Award record but no Irish CRO registration, incorporation date or company about-page could be found. The only firm date is a product launch: on the App Store by March 2010, winner of the 2010 UN World Summit Award Mobile.

name: Intheon
note: The company's own about page says only that it "was founded by pioneers in brain-computer interface and biosignal processing technology", with no year. Tracxn gives 2013 with founders Nima Bigdely-Shamlo, Tim Mullen and Allen Gruber; TheOrg and Crunchbase place Mullen's founder-CEO role start at 2015. The likely explanation is that Intheon was formerly Qusp or Syntrogi, making 2013 the predecessor's founding and 2015 the rename. Genuinely in scope: real-time EEG source imaging and artifact removal middleware, deeply tied to UCSD's Swartz Center, with CTO Christian Kothe the author of Lab Streaming Layer. A California Secretary of State search would settle it.

name: Neurolief
note: Three aggregator years and no primary statement: Startup Nation Central says August 2013, Tracxn 2012, PrivCo 2014, so none is recorded. Real neurotech — Relivion delivers non-invasive occipital and trigeminal nerve stimulation and received FDA PMA approval in January 2026 for at-home therapy in treatment-resistant depression. neurolief.com now redirects to prolivrx.com and the product trades as Proliv Rx; the company still exists with Amit Dar as founder and CTO. LOCATION: sources place HQ in Netanya or Herzliya, not Yoqne'am Illit.

name: Savonix
note: savonix.com now redirects to footyrankings.com — the domain has been dropped and resold to a football rankings site, which strongly suggests the company is defunct. Aggregators split 2014 against 2015 and the only firm dated event is a $5.1M Series A in June 2017, a funding round. The business was genuine: mobile digital neurocognitive assessment founded by Dr Mylea Charvat in San Francisco.

name: JoyHaptics
note: joyhaptics.com has been resold and now serves an online casino affiliate page; the company page 404s. The year 2015 survives only in indexed content of that lost page — "with JoyHaptics beginning in 2015", founders Dr Jussi Tuovinen and Kai Martesuo — so no year is recorded. JoyHaptics Oy of Helsinki is almost certainly defunct, though the Finnish trade register was not reachable to confirm. SCOPE: the iXu plush "smart bear" transmitted stroking motion between paired bears on a C-tactile afferent rationale — a consumer toy with a sensory-neuroscience story.

name: Blink Device Company
note: A company release of 26 April 2018 calls it "a recently formed medical device company", which is soft language rather than a stated year, and Bloomberg gives 2018. But the Washington Secretary of State lists BLINK DEVICE, LLC as a foreign LLC formed in DELAWARE on 15 July 2020 — after the October 2018 product launch — so 2018 is contradicted and probably describes a predecessor or a restructuring. No year is recorded. The row also points at a product page: TwitchView is the product, the company now trades as Blink Anesthesia, and TwitchView launched 10 October 2018 at the ASA meeting. SCOPE: a quantitative train-of-four monitor using electromyography at the neuromuscular junction — peripheral motor endplate function, not brain or CNS.

name: Mediagnost
note: Year recorded as 1985, well sourced. SCOPE: ELISA and immunoassay kits for infectiology (hepatitis A, Pseudomonas aeruginosa antibodies) and endocrinology (growth factors, leptin, resistin). An ISO 13485 IVD manufacturer with no nervous-system product line. LOCATION: founded in Tuebingen; Reutlingen is the current technology-park address.

name: Keystone Heart
note: Year recorded as 2004, aggregator-only. Renamed from SMT Research & Development Ltd in 2012 and acquired by Venus Medtech of Hangzhou for roughly $100M, merger completed 26 December 2018, so it is now a subsidiary rather than an independent Israeli company. SCOPE: the genuinely debatable case in its batch — TriGUARD 3 is deployed in the aortic arch and its clinical endpoint is reducing embolic lesions, stroke and neurocognitive decline, but it is cardiovascular hardware that never touches the nervous system.

name: Blazepod
note: Year recorded as 2015, contested and aggregator-only. LOCATION: the company is Play Coyotta Ltd of 30 Lilienblum Street, Tel Aviv-Jaffa; Miami is a US sales entity, BlazePod Inc. SCOPE: Bluetooth light pods that flash and detect taps, driving reaction and agility drills through a phone app — sports and fitness equipment. It measures reaction time as a behavioural output, as a stopwatch does. Its appearance in a reliability study as a response-time tool and its marketing to neurological therapists are the entire neuro connection.

name: Northstar Neuroscience
note: Year recorded as 1999, for the original name Vertis Neuroscience. The board voted to wind down and liquidate after the EVEREST pivotal trial missed its primary endpoint in January 2008, and the company CLOSED on 2 July 2009. The index's "https://n/a" website is accurate — there is nothing to link to.

name: Cogstate Ltd.
note: Year recorded as 1999 from the company's own about page. LOCATION: an Australian company headquartered at 367 Collins Street, Melbourne and listed on the ASX as CGS; New Haven and London are satellite offices, so the index records a branch as the origin. Still operating and independent. In scope: computerised language-neutral cognitive assessment for clinical trials and brain injury.

name: CIMHS - Centre for Interactive Mental Health Solutions
note: Year recorded as 2013. Self-described as "a not-for-profit organization... operated as a social business", founded and run by Kasra Zokaei in Toronto. Its product is Bliss, a free eight-session online CBT programme for depression launched September 2013. SCOPE: web-delivered psychotherapy content with no device, signal acquisition or nervous-system measurement. Unrelated to Beating the Blues, a different UK computerised-CBT product.

name: Long Good
note: Year recorded as 2011. The proper name is LongGood MediTech, Chinese 龍骨王; "Long Good" is a shortened anglicised form. Taipei location correct. It describes itself as the first Taiwanese developer of an interactive telerehabilitation system, expanding to Singapore in 2016. Serves neurological rehabilitation alongside musculoskeletal and orthopaedic, so partly in scope.

name: WellTrack
note: Year recorded as 2010. ACQUIRED by ProtoCall Services of Portland, Oregon in April 2020, so the independent Fredericton company no longer exists and the product is now WellTrack Boost. The legal name was CyberPsyc Software Solutions Inc. SCOPE: a CBT and mood-tracking self-help app for university students — no sensing.

name: Nibs
note: Year recorded as 2014, aggregator-only. The entity is effectively now QuantalX Neuroscience Ltd under the same founder and CEO Iftach Dolev; DELPhI became the Delphi-MD system, FDA De Novo authorised November 2025. Aggregators list the old name as deadpooled while mapping its slug to QuantalX, so this is a rename and continuation rather than a death. LOCATION: Ramat Gan, not Zur Moshe. Genuinely in scope: TMS-EEG based brain-network assessment.

name: Wazi
note: Year recorded as 2018 and disputed against mid-2020. SCOPE: teletherapy — a chatbot and web app connecting Kenyan users anonymously to licensed human therapists, plus white-label programmes for NGOs and governments. No brain or neural sensing; the only measurement is clinically validated questionnaire scoring. Backed by Founders Factory Africa, Kepple Africa Ventures, the Skoll Foundation and the Segal Family Foundation.

name: hiMoment
note: Year recorded as 2016, aggregator-grade. The company filed for Konkurs in Austria with no continuation planned; social activity stopped in April 2019 and the last press is July 2019. It had raised a 250k euro seed plus a 100k angel cheque after appearing on 2 Minuten 2 Millionen, reportedly never closed. SCOPE: a savouring-method gratitude journalling app with an algorithmic recommender — marketing claims neuroscience, but it is a diary.

name: Clutch Cognition
note: Year recorded as 2019 from the Danish CVR register. SCOPE: it trades as Clutch Nutrition and sells Clutch Mindset, a plant-based caffeine-free functional drink pitched as a nootropic alternative to energy drinks, after appearing on the Danish Dragons' Den. The nervous-system connection is a marketing claim about ingredients; there is no device, sensing or measurement. Included on the word "Cognition". Clutch Nutrition ApS appears against the same CVR, so a rename is likely.

name: HumanCharger
note: Year recorded as 2007. HumanCharger is the product — a bright-light earbud delivering light through the ear canal — and the company was Valkee Oy of Oulu, which filed for bankruptcy on 22 November 2021 per Yle. The product was taken over in 2022 by Humancharger.com ApS in the Copenhagen area, which now owns and sells it. So the founding year belongs to a dead Finnish company and the index's Oulu location is now wrong.

name: Tactical Information Systems
note: Year recorded as 2009, aggregator-only and unverified. SCOPE: a defence and law-enforcement biometrics contractor doing cloud-hosted fingerprint, palmprint, face and iris matching for governments, border security and conflict-zone deployment. No nervous-system connection whatsoever; it appears in aggregators under the slug beehive-biometrics. tacticalinfosys.com fails TLS entirely, the last notable press is IBM SmartCamp 2011, and with six listed employees it may no longer operate.

name: DrOmnibus
note: Year recorded as 2013 from Startup Poland, a national association rather than a register; the Polish KRS was not checked. SCOPE: ABA DrOmnibus is applied behaviour analysis therapy software for children with autism, Down syndrome and ADHD, split into practitioner and parent editions — behavioural therapy software rather than instrumented neurotechnology. First European company into the Google Launchpad Accelerator, 2017 cohort. dromnibus.com failed to load on repeated attempts, so trading status is unconfirmed.

name: Breathwrk
note: Year recorded as 2019, aggregator-only. SCOPE: a consumer breathing-exercise app for stress and anxiety with habit programmes and audio and visual pacing cues. The autonomic-nervous-system framing is real but there is no sensing and no device — a wellness app.

name: Cupcake Sweet Entertainment
note: Year recorded as 2012, aggregator-only. SCOPE: a mobile games studio building free-to-play casual word and puzzle titles — Letters of Gold, Words of Gold, Numbers of Gold — which raised $1M from Playlab of Thailand in February 2017. There is no measurement, stimulation or nervous-system technology; it appears to have been swept in on the phrase "brain puzzle games". It now trades as Cupcake Entertainment, so the index name is stale as well.

name: Braincare Health Tecnology
note: Year recorded as 2014 from Revista Pesquisa FAPESP. The row is stale and misspelled on two counts: the legal entity is Braincare Desenvolvimento e Inovacao Tecnologica S.A., it now trades as brain4care, and the index writes "Tecnology". A confirmed USP spin-off from Prof. Sergio Mascarenhas's research at the Sao Carlos Institute of Physics. Strong fit: non-invasive intracranial pressure and compliance monitoring, with trials running in Brazil's public health system.

name: Medsurant Health
note: Year recorded as 2009, aggregator-only. ACQUIRED by MPOWERHealth in January 2025; its own site now renders the logo as "an mpowerhealth company". The parent holding entity is Medsurant Holdings, LLC, operating seven subsidiary practices including American Intraoperative Monitoring across twenty states. SCOPE: it supplies technologists and supervising neurologists who perform intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring, onsite or by remote supervision, and develops no hardware or software of its own — a clinical services and staffing business.

name: VascularFX
note: ww5.micrusendovascular.com returns NXDOMAIN — the ww5. prefix is a parking-service signature and the underlying domain is gone entirely. VascularFX was real but has not existed independently for 21 years: Micrus Endovascular acquired it in July 2005 for about $4M and its IP became the ENZO steerable microcatheter; Micrus was itself acquired by Johnson & Johnson and Codman in 2010. Any year attached to that domain would belong to Micrus. SCOPE: catheters and guidewires for accessing cerebral vasculature — neurovascular hardware rather than a neural interface.

name: Strokelab
note: strokelab.ch returns NXDOMAIN and no evidence was found that a Swiss company called Strokelab exists or ever existed. Searching the name returns only unrelated things: the Stroke Research Center Bern, an academic centre founded 2020 at the University of Bern from the Departments of Neurology, Neurosurgery and Neuroradiology; a Japanese rehabilitation clinic chain branded STROKE LAB; a genomics repository; and a golf putter technology. The Bern location is consistent with the university centre, so this row may be an academic research centre miscatalogued as a company.

name: Neuro-Medware
note: neuromedware.com returns NXDOMAIN. The only source carrying a year is F6S, which served a bot-verification wall on direct fetch, so its 2020 figure comes from a search engine's cached rendering rather than a page anyone read. The full name appears to be BT Neuro-MedWare. Context that does check out: the venture is connected to Dr Richi Gill, a Calgary bariatric surgeon paralysed in a 2018 accident who received epidural spinal stimulation implants, which makes it plausibly in scope — but there is no company website, no registry entry and no news naming a founding year.

name: DEEP
note: This row is a mashup of two unrelated things. exploredeep.com is DEEP VR, a breathing-controlled meditative VR experience — a project with no legal entity, no incorporation, no headquarters and no founding year, begun by Owen Harris in Ireland and developed with Dutch designer Niki Smit after they met in the summer of 2014, with efficacy research run since 2016 with the GEMH Lab at Radboud. The "Shefayim, Israel" location in the index belongs to a completely different company also called DEEP, an AI content-automation firm near Tel Aviv. Do not merge them.

name: Supportiv
note: Aggregators say 2012 but all press and product evidence points to 2017-2018: the service was in stealth from January 2018 and launched publicly that June. A six-year gap between a claimed founding and stealth-mode operation is implausible and could not be reconciled. supportiv.com/about-us is a 404 and the Columbia Business School portfolio page returned 403. Real and operating, founded by Helena Plater-Zyberk and Pouria Mojabi. SCOPE: anonymous live-moderated peer-support chat with NLP topic routing — no neural measurement.

name: Precise Cardiology Limited
note: By its own wording the entity was "registered in Hong Kong on 7 November 2017 with the objective of creating a specific and separate corporate entity to hold and develop the PRECISE Cloud ECG product" — an incorporation date for a product-holding vehicle, with Planexta Inc. of California holding 95% of initial share capital and being the real originator. No year is recorded. precisecloud.online returns NXDOMAIN. SCOPE: cloud-based ECG interpretation. The only thread to the nervous system is heart-rate-variability analysis as an autonomic proxy.

name: Void
note: void.com.hk is live and serves "Void 人類圖", a HUMAN DESIGN training school — an astrology-adjacent personality system — selling three tiers of certification courses across Taiwan and Hong Kong. It has no nervous-system connection whatsoever and is a textbook name-collision entry. Its site claims establishment in 2015, which is self-reported marketing copy from that school and must not be carried into a neurotech index. Searching "Void Hong Kong" also returns a Central nightclub and a meditation app, so the row may have been intended for something else entirely.

name: Brain Fingerprinting Laboratories
note: No source states a founding year. The only hard anchor is SEC EDGAR CIK 1175489, a Form REGDEX paper filing for FY2002, which establishes only that the company existed and was raising capital by 2002. Popular articles imply about 1991 by saying Farwell had run it "12 years" as of 2003 — arithmetic from a relative phrase, refused. 1991 is the Farwell and Donchin publication and 1995 the patent; both date the TECHNIQUE, not the company, and are routinely conflated. Genuinely EEG and P300 based. Do not confuse with Brainwave Science, a separate 2012 Farwell venture that ended in mutual fraud allegations.

name: Anxiety Reliever
note: anxietyrelieverapp.com returns NXDOMAIN. This is a consumer mobile app rather than a company: an iOS listing whose ID range implies a 2015-era App Store registration and a Google Play listing, associated with an individual designer rather than an incorporated entity. The strongest date signal is a personal portfolio page titled "Anxiety Reliever App (2016-2019)" — a project date range, not a founding. SCOPE: a self-help relaxation app with no measurement or stimulation.

name: NeuroRoots
note: An academic research project and a device name from a paper, not a company. NeuroRoots is a bio-inspired axon-mimicking flexible multi-electrode brain-machine interface — roughly 7-10 micrometres wide and 1.5 thick, delivered on a retractable tungsten microwire — developed by Marc D. Ferro and Nicholas A. Melosh in Materials Science at Stanford. The index's "website" is the bioRxiv preprint itself, posted 4 November 2018; the work was later published in AIP Advances in 2024. No company website, no incorporation, no spin-out. The Stanford location is the correct lab affiliation.

name: Neuronics
note: A ROBOTICS company: Neuronics AG made the Katana lightweight human-safe collaborative robot arm, reportedly founded 2001 as a spin-off of the Artificial Intelligence Lab at the University of Zurich by Dr Hansruedi Fruh. The "neuro" refers to neural-network AI, not the nervous system, so no year is recorded here. neuronics.ch redirects to a Sedo parking and sales lander, the Katana was discontinued and press stops around 2009. The same name-not-business failure mode as Medibrane and DataNovo.

name: Neurobit Technologies
note: TWO unrelated companies share this name and the index row matches the one this brief did not describe. Neurobit Technologies Co., Ltd. of Taiwan makes smart glasses recording nystagmus waveforms. Neurobit Technologies Pte Ltd of Singapore is the arm of Neurobit Health, HQ New York, doing AI auto-scoring of polysomnography — sleep, not eye movements. The row (neurobit.io, Jalan Besar, Singapore) matches the SLEEP company. Neither states a founding year on its site. The row's URL is also a resold chain: neurobit.io redirects to ee88.channel, which redirects to aerodata.in.

name: Neurogenic
note: Neurogenic Ltd. of Israel is real and in scope: a clinical-stage ELISA immunoassay for platelet-associated antibodies to diagnose early-onset schizophrenia, with science tracing to Prof. Meir Shinitzky at the Weizmann Institute and a 2019 antibody deal with SYnAbs. But the only temporal hooks are unusable — the site says "Over the past 25 years, Neurogenic has been collaborating with colleagues from the Weizmann Institute", a relative phrase that was refused, and a director bio says Yossi Avnat has served "since its inception" with no date. Start-Up Nation Central returned 403; the Israeli Registrar of Companies would settle it.

name: Medtronicdbs
note: Not an entity. medtronicdbs.co.in fails DNS entirely — not parked, not 404, it does not resolve — and the hostname appears in no search result, press item or filing anywhere. A .co.in domain bearing Medtronic's trademark plus a product-line abbreviation is at best a regional marketing microsite for Medtronic plc's deep brain stimulation line; Medtronic's actual Indian DBS content lives at medtronic.com/in-en. The listed "Dublin, Ireland" is Medtronic plc's registered HQ and flatly contradicts a .co.in domain, which suggests the row was generated by pattern-matching the Medtronic name. This is the THIRD Medtronic row in the index, after "Medtronic" and "Medtronic Vascular".

name: iCouch
note: Vendor directories assert "founded in 2010" but none could be opened, and icouch.me itself fails TLS negotiation on both / and /about, so the company's own words were never read. The only date surfaced is a product one: iCouch released the first version of its video platform in 2010. No year is recorded. SCOPE: HIPAA-compliant practice-management software for therapists — scheduling, video, client notes, invoicing and file storage. A SaaS booking and billing product for talk-therapy practices.

name: PixelAtion Labs
note: pixelationlabs.com has an expired TLS certificate and could not be fetched. The only company-register hit is PIXELATION LABS PTE. LTD. of Singapore, incorporated 13 May 2022, which is not obviously the Tarzana, California outfit the index means and whose date must not be transferred. The Tarzana entity appears to be a small iOS studio making autism and ABA behaviour-support apps — the "This for That" series of visual schedules, token boards and timers. SCOPE: special-education software with no EEG or neural measurement.

name: MyBrainTest
note: An information and review website, not a technology developer. mybraintest.org self-describes as "an online brain health and wellness resource" providing "an independent source of information on brain health screening tests", publishing free screening tools and comparison reports on OTHER companies' cognitive screening products; one third-party profile characterises it as a market-research and advisory service for the neurodiagnostic industry. Despite the .org there is no evidence of nonprofit registration, no named individual or company, and WHOIS is privacy-redacted. The oldest dated post path is 2015 and a scanner reports the domain as roughly 15 years old; neither is a founding year.

name: Picto Connection
note: Gust says September 2014; the only reputable news source, Valencia Plaza of 3 March 2015, describes the software as presented "less than fifteen days" earlier and the company as newly constituted by creator Meritxell Molina, then 22 — pointing at 2014-2015 with neither confirmable against a register. The BORME record returned 403. LOCATION: Valencian in origin, listed under Barcelona because it relocated there for the Incubio incubator. SCOPE: an AAC pictogram app for autism and stroke-related aphasia; its "neurological test" is an onboarding questionnaire. pictoconnection.com fails with an SSL protocol error.

name: Goodrich International
note: A SHOE company. Goodrich International is genuinely the parent of High Beam Shoes of Dallas, run by Joe Goodrich Sr. and Jr., selling shoes with built-in LED headlights for runners, dog-walkers and children's night safety. There is no nervous-system connection whatsoever. The only neuro link is the founder's mother's ALS diagnosis in late 2013, mentioned in marketing copy as the motivation for starting the business, which is almost certainly why an automated scrape pulled it in. The "2013" in that copy refers to the product idea and no Texas registry record was found, so no year is recorded.

name: Mantaray AR
note: mantarayar.com returns NXDOMAIN — the domain has lapsed entirely and the only surviving presence is an abandoned WordPress blog. Mantaray AR LLC did exist: an Arizona software company making no-code augmented-reality authoring for classrooms plus "Paugme", an app to teach empathy to people with autism, announced 12 June 2014. LOCATION: that 2014 announcement gives Tempe, not the Winkelman the index and Crunchbase carry. SCOPE: classroom AR authoring with one autism-adjacent app; no sensing or neural measurement.

name: Puzzle Piece
note: No founding year on the company site or in any news source. The nearest datable events are a $100k seed dated 5 May 2015 and TechCrunch coverage of the $19 tablet in the same era, neither of which is a founding. The original business was a $19 custom Android tablet preloaded with autism-education apps on a subscription model, co-founded by Andrea Macken, BCBA, in Murrieta. The site has been hollowed out: getpuzzlepiece.com now pushes an Amazon Fire HD Kids bundle as an affiliate page. Aggregator data is contaminated by several unrelated organisations sharing the name.

name: Brainsview
note: No sourced founding year after three searches. Real and in scope: BrainsView Inc. of Ontario makes hardware and software for real-time brain monitoring of brain injury, and the Ontario Brain Institute lists it as a portfolio company described as "Neuropathology Monitor" — which confirms existence but gives no date. brainsview.com is HTTP-only and fails its TLS handshake so it cannot be fetched. LOCATION: Crunchbase places it in Mississauga rather than the Toronto the index records. A 2016 NeuroTech Ontario Showcase appearance is a floor, not a founding.

name: Play2Focus
note: Could not be established to exist. The index stores the literal string "https://N/A" so there is no site to check, and two searches returned no company matching the row. The only "Play2Focus" on the open web is a GTD task-management app with no nervous-system connection and no Hong Kong link. Everything else returned is a different entity — Playfocus the game studio, PLAYfocus the Hong Kong childcare service, or Play Attention the US attention-training system, which is a plausible source of confusion. Hong Kong neurofeedback providers that do exist are clinics.

name: MotusXR
note: motusxr.com returns HTTP 404 and Tracxn marks the company deadpooled. Aggregators give 2018 with founders Ian Dawson and Louisa Spring, but F6S served a bot-check and Tracxn is paywalled, so that is search-snippet hearsay and no year is recorded. The business was a motion-disorders telehealth research platform using lightweight motion capture for remote clinical research — in scope, though motion capture rather than a brain interface. Note one aggregator renders the location as "Louisa (United States)", which is the co-founder's first name misparsed as a city; do not propagate it.

name: Eleos Health
note: Year recorded as 2020, disputed against 2019. SCOPE: AI documentation and voice and NLP analysis of therapy sessions for behavioural health providers. It touches no neural signal. Roughly $126M raised across a Series C, HQ split Boston and Tel Aviv.

name: SpellBound
note: Year recorded as 2016, with 2015 defensible. The legal entity is ALTality, Inc.; SpellBound is the trading and product brand. Founder and CEO Christina York, Ann Arbor. SCOPE: augmented-reality distraction and procedure-simulation games for paediatric patients, including an AR MRI simulator — behavioural pain-distraction software with no neural component.

name: Bioimmunate
note: Year recorded as 2014, aggregator-only. bioimmunate.com now redirects to expireddomains.com — the domain has lapsed and is listed as expired, a strong signal the company is dead or dormant, with no news after the mid-2010s. SCOPE: engineered particles removing autoreactive immune cells from blood before they reach the CNS; the only nervous-system link is the multiple sclerosis indication.

name: Prospect Bio
note: Year recorded as 2013, aggregator-only, with PitchBook recording operations ceased as of 1 January 2020. SCOPE: living-cell biosensors detecting industrial small molecules for flavour and fragrance, agriculture and nutrition. No nervous-system connection of any kind. prospect.bio is parked for sale.

name: Karmagenes
note: Year recorded as 2015 from the Swiss register. SCOPE: consumer genomics — a saliva DNA test scoring loci claimed to relate to personality and behaviour traits, sold direct to consumers and latterly bundled with psychometrics. Behavioural-genetics marketing is not a nervous-system technology, and the scientific basis for DNA-based personality scoring is contested.

name: DYNSEO
note: Year recorded as 2013 from the French register. SCOPE: a publisher of cognitive-stimulation game apps for seniors, dementia patients and speech therapists, sold to care homes. No sensing, no neural interface, no signal processing. Its closest claim is MedappCare certification of one app and a 15-person adoption study.

name: HealthRhythms
note: Year recorded as 2014. LOCATION: consistently described as New York-based with a Cornell Tech lineage, not the Boston the index records. healthrhythms.com/about is a 404 so the year comes from trade press. In scope in a way most of its batch is not: passive smartphone sensing producing mental-health digital biomarkers.

name: Braincare
note: Year recorded as 2014. CONFIRMED DUPLICATE of "Braincare Health Tecnology": the same USP Sao Carlos spin-off founded by Sergio Mascarenhas, Gustavo Frigieri and Rodrigo Andrade, doing non-invasive intracranial pressure and cranial-compliance monitoring via a headband sensor. It traded as Braincare and rebranded to brain4care. Merge, keeping brain4care as the current name.

name: Lift Labs
note: Year recorded as 2010, weakly. ACQUIRED by Google in September 2014 and folded into Google X life sciences, which became Verily, where Liftware still sits; Lift Labs no longer exists independently and liftlabsdesign.com is stale. Liftware is the product — a self-stabilising spoon for essential tremor and Parkinson's — and Lift Labs the company.

name: Oncovision
note: Year recorded as 2003. LOCATION: oncovision.com is General Equipment for Medical Imaging S.A., known as GEM Imaging, headquartered in VALENCIA, SPAIN with a Boston office; the index says Mexico City, which is at best a sales presence. SCOPE: an oncology nuclear-imaging manufacturer whose single nervous-system product, CareMiBRAIN, is the entire neurotech justification.

name: Autism Training Solutions
note: Year recorded as 2010, from the co-founder's biography. ACQUIRED by Relias Learning, completed 12 June 2014; it no longer exists independently and its content folded into Relias's ABA library. SCOPE: e-learning and workforce training content about applied behaviour analysis — no device, no measurement.

name: Purple Gaze
note: Year recorded as 2019, aggregator-only with no primary or registry backing. LOCATION: the company's own site gives Winthontlaan 200, Utrecht — not the Amsterdam the index records. FOXIE is a portable high-speed eye tracker with Python experiment software sold to vision-science researchers: legitimately neuro-adjacent oculomotor measurement, but not a brain interface.

name: MoreMemo
note: Year recorded as 2020 from the Danish CVR register. SCOPE: a remote-controlled tablet for elderly and cognitively impaired users, where relatives manage video calls, photos, messages and alerts from their own phones. Assistive eldercare consumer software; neurotech only in a dementia-adjacent sense.

name: Muse
note: Year recorded as 2007. Muse is the EEG meditation headband; the company is InteraXon Inc. of Toronto, which now trades publicly under the Muse brand — Businesswire releases are headed "Interaxon Inc. (Muse)". The row should name InteraXon. Product development began 2003 and the headband launched 2014; neither is the founding.

name: Neuraltide
note: Year recorded as 2017, an incorporation date. French registry-data sites report a simplified judicial liquidation pronounced 5 September 2025 with cessation of payments 30 June 2025, and founder Karine Berthet replaced as president in November 2023. This was not verified directly against an official register — treat as strong but unconfirmed. The website is still up.

name: MicroPort (Shanghai)
note: Year recorded as 1998, for MicroPort Scientific Corporation (853.HK) — a large general medical device conglomerate that began in interventional cardiology and IPO'd in Hong Kong in September 2010. The neurovascular business is MicroPort NeuroTech (2172.HK), a separately listed entity with its own much later founding. If the index wants the neuro business, this row points at the wrong entity.

name: Avaz
note: Year recorded as 2007. CONFIRMED DUPLICATE of the "Invention Labs" row: Avaz is the AAC app brand and Invention Labs Engineering Products Private Limited of Chennai, IIT Madras incubated, is the originator. Two complications: the about page now brands the entity "Avaz Inc.", so the brand was elevated to company name at some point; and Avaz is now part of the PRC-Saltillo family. The 2007 date belongs to the Indian originator.

name: Strohl Medical
note: Year recorded as 2009, aggregator-only and probably all deriving from one self-reported profile. strohlmedical.com returns no content and the trail stops around 2012 after a $245k debt round; founder Heather Keith has moved on to Anivia Medical. In scope: NeuroEPG, an evoked-potential device for rapid stroke triage in the ED. A Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth search would settle both the founding and the dissolution.

name: Intratech Medical
note: Year recorded as 2007, aggregator-only. intratechmedical.com returns no content and development looks complete, so the company may be dormant or wound down. LOCATION: sources say it moved from Netanya to the Shefayim Commercial Center. In scope: NAVIMAX, a spiral balloon over-the-wire catheter for clot retrieval in acute ischaemic stroke, CE marked May 2014.

name: Neural-FLEX
note: Year recorded as 2018. The English name corresponds to 易念科技（深圳）有限公司, founder Feng Chao, confirmed by an exact address match between the registry record and the company site. neu-flex.com returned HTTP 521 on every attempt, so the site is at minimum flaky. In scope: the SOULINK non-invasive EEG headband, EEG and EMG wearables and depression-warning models.

name: Oncomfort
note: Year recorded as 2017. ACQUIRED by HypnoVR of Strasbourg in October 2023 — and HypnoVR is itself a row in this index, so the two rows describe one company from that date. LOCATION: Wavre, not Brussels, per its own boilerplate. oncomfort.com fails DNS. SCOPE: VR "Digital Sedation" for procedural pain and anxiety via clinical hypnosis — a behavioural VR therapeutic rather than a neural interface.

name: Nuro Corp
note: Year recorded as 2017, labelled incorporation by the company itself. The live site is nuro.world, not the indexed nuro.ca. In scope: a non-surgical BCI for communication and computer control in severe neurological impairment — ALS, stroke, disorders of consciousness — with the product Gridly. Not to be confused with Nuro, Inc., the Mountain View autonomous-delivery company.

name: Mr. Doc
note: Year recorded as 2018, an Italian registration date. SCOPE: AI diagnostics from noisy consumer-device signals across arrhythmias, hypertension, asthma, COPD and Parkinson's, plus retinal OCT inflammation detection. The nervous-system connection is thin and incidental. Two similarly named Rome entities exist and only one was matched to the CORDIS coordinator record; the LinkedIn slug suggests a rebrand to Cardiia, unverified.

name: Psicologia Viva
note: Year recorded as 2015, with the CNPJ suggesting a 2017 incorporation. SCOPE: an online psychotherapy marketplace connecting patients to human psychologists by video. No device, no signal acquisition, no nervous-system technology — a keyword-driven inclusion. MERGED with Conexa Saude in March 2021, so no longer independent.

name: Bionic Vision Technologies
